cadence_evidence.value: Spatial grain is the 2DDI (depth-integrated) unstructured FE mesh exercised by this binding; the optional 3D (IM=21) mode is "3-D" but is not covered by the HydroCraft 2DDI tooling. Time stepping is sub-hourly finite-difference (DTDP ~0.5-10 s, CFL-limited). The GWCE is a mass-conserving continuity formulation, so closure is mass-balance (the 3D transport mode additionally conserves the advected scalar/heat budget). The hydrostatic pressure and Boussinesq approximations are governing simplifications of the momentum equations, recorded here rather than in the closure field.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass and momentum are conserved by the Godunov-type finite-volume scheme over unstructured triangular cells. Timestepping is adaptive and CFL-constrained (dt <= CFL * min(dx/sqrt(g*h)) across all triangles); the user-set yieldstep only governs output cadence, not the stable inner timestep. Wetting/drying clips depth to zero where stage < bed elevation; the balance_deep_and_shallow / protect_against_infinitesimal_and_negative_heights limiters redistribute momentum and clamp negative heights outside the explicit flux step.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure applies to water (PCP ~= WYLD + ET + DPRK + delta-S within about +/-5%) and to N, P, C, sediment, and pesticides; channel routing conserves mass between subareas to the outlet. Most processes run daily; optional Green-Ampt infiltration and rainfall-excess are computed at sub-daily (~0.1 h) intervals. ET options are demand-side flux calculations, not a closed surface energy budget.

cadence_evidence.value: Daily mass bookkeeping across coupled modules: crop returns soil water and N uptake to the soil water/N modules each day, crop cover passed to the water balance for evaporation/runoff, and tops/root residues passed to surface-organic-matter and soil N at harvest. The soil profile is solved consecutively (process-by-process) each day, not as simultaneous coupled flow equations. MicroClimate computes a Penman-Monteith / equilibrium-evaporation energy balance for potential ET, but the overall conservation target is water and C/N mass, not a closed surface energy budget.

source_evidence.value: Solar radiation supplied in W/m² instead of MJ/m²/day; ERA5 ssrd is in J/m²/day (divide by 1e6). CMFD srad is often in W/m² (multiply by 0.0864). If radiation column values are 100-400 instead of 5-30, the units are wrong. APSIM interprets each value as MJ/m², so 200 W/m² becomes 200 MJ/m² — about 8

Temperature supplied in Kelvin instead of Celsius; ERA5 and some reanalysis products report temperature in Kelvin. APSIM expects Celsius. 300 K = 27°C. If left unconverted, APSIM interprets 300°C, causing thermal time to accumulate at extreme rates.
; ['Weather', 'Phenology', 'MicroClimate']

Soil layer thickness in cm instead of mm; APSIM expects Thickness array in mm. HWSD and SoilGrids report depths in cm. A 30 cm layer entered as 30 (without conversion) becomes 30 mm (3 cm). A 5-layer profile of [15,15,30,40,50] cm becomes 150 mm total instead of 1500 mm.
; ['Physical', 'Root', 'Wate

Bulk density in kg/m³ instead of g/cc; SoilGrids reports BD in kg/m³ (e.g., 1400). APSIM expects g/cc (e.g., 1.4). If 1400 is entered directly, APSIM may crash or produce nonsensical water balance results since BD is used to compute porosity.
; ['Physical', 'WaterBalance']

Sub-daily rainfall (mm/3hr) not summed to daily totals; CMFD and some ERA5 products provide rainfall at 3-hourly intervals. APSIM requires daily totals. Using a single 3-hour interval as the daily value gives approximately 1/8 of actual rainfall.
; ['Weather', 'SoilWater']

Vapor pressure in kPa instead of hPa; APSIM expects VP in hPa. ERA5 often provides vapor pressure in kPa. 2.0 kPa = 20 hPa. If 2.0 is passed as hPa (very low VP), VPD is overestimated, inflating evapotranspiration.
; ['Weather', 'MicroClimate', 'Leaf']

cadence_evidence.value: Per-pixel 1-D mass-and-energy-balance closure; water and energy are conserved within each column. There is no lateral inter-column closure except wind-driven snow redistribution (SnowDrift) and radiative terrain exchange (EnergyBalance). The outer driver cadence is fixed at dt_main = 3600 s; CALCULATION_STEP_LENGTH only sets the SNOWPACK inner sub-step count, and sub-threshold precipitation is held in an internal accumulation store, so precipitation conservation holds over the accumulation window rather than strictly per timestep.

cadence_evidence.value: Water and sediment are mass-conserved on a uniform square-cell grid. The domain is closed except for rainfall input and exit through grid-edge cells; reported outlet discharge is summed over ALL boundary (edge) cells, so a multi-edge-outlet DEM over-reports outlet Q. Adaptive internal timestep (between min_time_step and max_time_step) is set by a Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy condition; the model resolves sub-second to hourly flow steps while simulated periods range from hours (floods) to thousands of years (landscape evolution). No surface energy budget is closed.

cadence_evidence.value: 2-D longitudinal-vertical (x-z) over a Waterbody->Branch->Segment(DLX)->Layer(H) grid; lateral dimension averaged out, quasi-3D only via branching. Governing equations are laterally and layer averaged in conservative form under the Boussinesq and hydrostatic approximations (vertical momentum neglected). Mass-balance closure applies to water volume and to each active constituent (heat/N/P/C accounting; ~1e-9 volume-balance tolerance in BALANCES). The surface energy budget is an equilibrium-temperature / term-by-term heat exchange (solar with BETA surface fraction and EXH2O attenuation, longwave back-radiation, evaporative + sensible via Bowen ratio, CBHE bottom exchange), so energy closure is the surface heat-flux balance rather than a fully resolved 3-D energy field. Timestep is auto-stepped for stability (DLT CON / DLTMIN floor); implicit free-surface and vertical diffusion remove gravity-wave and vertical-diffusion stability limits.

cadence_evidence.value: Solves conservation of mass, energy, and momentum on a structured x/y grid with vertical sigma layers. Mass-balance closure governs ice thickness; energy closure governs the prognostic temperature/enthalpy field; momentum is solved diagnostically each step via a stress-balance approximation (SIA in Glide; Blatter-Pattyn/SSA/L1L2/DIVA in Glissade). Internal state uses SI units (m/s) while netCDF output applies a seconds-per-year scaling (scyr) to emit m/yr.

cadence_evidence.value: Each grid cell/tile is an independent 1-D vertical column (configurable ground layers; standard offline config is 20 layers to >61 m depth); gridded runs are many independent columns with no lateral exchange. CLASS physics runs at a sub-daily timestep (15 min coupled, 30 min offline); CTEM biogeochemistry runs daily. Closure is dual: surface energy budget closure is enforced by construction (unlike eddy-covariance towers with 10-30% residual), and the terrestrial carbon budget closes (NEE/NEP sums to zero at equilibrium) only when spinfast=1 — accelerated soil-carbon spin-up (spinfast>1) deliberately breaks the carbon mass balance.

fields.name: SWAN spectral resolution (direction / frequency bins)

cadence_evidence.value: ROMS conserves mass (volume/tracer) and momentum on a split-explicit free surface; the barotropic mode is sub-cycled NDTFAST times per baroclinic DT. Air-sea energy closure holds only when bulk fluxes (COARE) or WRF coupling supplies the surface heat/momentum budget; with prescribed-flux forcing the surface budget is imposed, not closed. Inter-component exchange is conservative only to the accuracy of the SCRIP remap weights between non-coincident component grids. Sediment bed mass is conserved within the morphodynamic accounting when the sediment module is active.

fields.name: T2
fields.notes: 2-m air temperature; valid 223.16-316.16 K. Celsius input silently forces 100% rain in the tanh snow/rain partition.

fields.name: RH2
fields.notes: 2-m relative humidity. Supplying a 0-1 fraction collapses latent heat flux to ~0.

fields.name: U2
fields.notes: Wind speed expected at the 2-m measurement height z; 10-m reanalysis wind without log-profile correction overestimates turbulent fluxes.

fields.name: G
fields.notes: Instantaneous incoming shortwave; valid 0-1600. Accumulated J m^-2 is ~3600x too high.

fields.name: PRES
fields.notes: Surface air pressure; Pa input makes air density and turbulent fluxes ~100x too large.

fields.name: RRR
fields.notes: Total (liquid+solid) precipitation per timestep; the model uses the raw value and does NOT divide by dt. Required unless SNOWFALL supplied.

fields.name: N
fields.notes: Cloud cover, used to parametrize incoming longwave when LWin is absent. Required unless LWin given; percent input inflates LWin.

fields.name: LWin
fields.notes: Optional measured incoming longwave; when absent it is parametrized from T2, RH2 (vapour pressure) and N via a Konzelmann-type clear-sky emissivity blended with an overcast term.

fields.name: SNOWFALL
fields.notes: Optional direct snowfall as SNOW HEIGHT (not w.e.); units differ from the w.e. SNOWFALL output. mm or m-w.e. input creates hundreds of layers and hits max_layers.

fields.name: albedo_fresh_snow / albedo_firn / albedo_ice
fields.notes: Endpoint albedos (defaults 0.85 / 0.55 / 0.30) for the aging decay.

fields.name: albedo decay timescales
fields.notes: Snow-aging and depth-decay timescales of the Oerlemans98 / Bougamont05 schemes.

fields.name: roughness lengths (fresh snow / firn / ice)
fields.notes: Moelg12 interpolates z0 between surface types by snow age; constant for ice, time-dependent for snow. Code divides the Moelg result by 1000 (mm->m).

fields.name: snow/rain transfer temperature threshold and spread
fields.notes: Center/width of the tanh snow-fraction transfer function.

fields.name: densification coefficients (Boone / Vionnet / empirical)
fields.notes: Boone (c1=2.8e-6, eta0=3.7e7, rho0=150, ...) and Vionnet constants are hardcoded in-source, not in constants.toml.

fields.name: fresh-snow density coefficients
fields.notes: Empirical fit max(109 + 6*(T2-273.16) + 26*sqrt(U2), 50) with hardcoded coefficients and a 50 kg/m^3 floor; active unless densification_method=='constant'.

fields.name: Bintanja shortwave extinction coefficients (snow 17.1, ice 2.5)
fields.notes: Hardcoded extinction coefficients for subsurface shortwave penetration.

fields.name: thermal conductivity / heat-equation stability factor
fields.notes: Explicit-conduction Courant safety factor c_stab=0.8 hardcoded; conductivity derived per-layer in Node.

fields.name: turbulent Prandtl number
fields.notes: Pr=0.8 hardcoded in the Monin-Obukhov bulk flux scheme.

fields.name: remesh density/temperature thresholds
fields.notes: Merge thresholds (density_threshold_merging, merge_max) controlling adaptive layer merging.

fields.name: measurement height z
fields.notes: Height at which forcing is assumed representative (default 2.0 m).

fields.name: initial_snowheight_constant
fields.notes: Default 0.2 m; HIGH influence on first months. Zero snowheight with no early snowfall pins albedo at the ice value 0.3.

fields.name: initial_glacier_height
fields.notes: Default 40 m; assumed thick enough that the column does not melt through.

fields.name: initial_top_density_snowpack / initial_bottom_density_snowpack
fields.notes: Defaults 300 / 600 kg/m^3 setting the initial density profile.

fields.name: temperature_bottom
fields.notes: Bottom-boundary column temperature (default 270.16 K).

fields.name: initial_surface_temperature
fields.notes: Hardcoded 270.0 K seed for the across-timestep surface_temperature scalar; read by the Bougamont05 albedo decay and used as the first energy-balance iteration guess. Not in constants.toml. Distinct from temperature_bottom (270.16 K bottom-boundary column temperature).

fields.name: restart column state
fields.notes: Full layer-resolved heights/densities/temperatures/LWC from a spinup of >=1 year; recommended for production runs.

fields.name: MASK (glacier mask)
fields.notes: Only MASK=1 cells are simulated. All-zero mask yields empty output; NaN forcing in a MASK=1 cell aborts the run.

fields.name: HGT (elevation/DEM)
fields.notes: Elevation field defining the domain.

fields.name: SLOPE / ASPECT
fields.notes: Terrain slope and aspect (0=North); used for radiation geometry. Declared in the code/KI static set but not in the readthedocs static-field list.

fields.name: albedo_method
fields.notes: Oerlemans98 (default) vs Bougamont05 albedo evolution scheme.

fields.name: stability_correction
fields.notes: Ri (default) vs MO Monin-Obukhov stability correction for turbulent fluxes.

fields.name: densification_method
fields.notes: Boone (default) / Vionnet / empirical / constant compaction scheme.

fields.name: sfc_temperature_method
fields.notes: Secant (default) / L-BFGS-B / SLSQP solver for the surface energy balance; L-BFGS-B and SLSQP can give different (potentially wrong) results since a Feb 2024 update.

fields.name: remesh_method
fields.notes: log_profile (default, fast/smoothed) vs adaptive_profile (detailed, costlier) layer remeshing.

fields.name: dt (time step)
fields.notes: Default 3600 s; MUST equal input forcing resolution because all flux-to-mass conversions use raw per-step values.

fields.name: WRF dimension flag
fields.notes: Selects south_north/west_east WRF dimension names instead of lat/lon.

cadence_evidence.value: Energy and mass balance are solved jointly: the surface energy balance is iterated for a consistent skin temperature (constrained to T_s <= T_m = 273.16 K) and the subsurface obeys a per-layer continuity constraint theta_i + theta_w + theta_a = 1, so any net mass change is accompanied by changes in ice fraction, liquid water content, and porosity. The model is distributed over a gridded lat/lon domain but each cell is an independent 1-D vertical column with no lateral coupling. Default dt is 3600 s and MUST equal the input forcing temporal resolution (the model uses raw per-timestep values and does not divide by dt).
Total (liquid+solid) precipitation per timestep; the model uses the raw value and does NOT divide by dt. Required unless SNOWFALL supplied.
Default 0.2 m; HIGH influence on first months. Zero snowheight with no early snowfall pins albedo at the ice value 0.3.

Hardcoded 270.0 K seed for the across-timestep surface_temperature scalar; read by the Bougamont05 albedo decay and used as the first energy-balance iteration guess. Not in constants.toml. Distinct from temperature_bottom (270.16 K bottom-boundary column temperature).

Shortwave radiation in J/m2 (accumulated) instead of W/m2 (instantaneous); ERA5 provides shortwave radiation as accumulated J/m2 per accumulation period. To get W/m2, divide by the number of seconds in the accumulation period. If raw J/m2 values (e.g., 3.6e6 = 1000 W/m2 * 3600s) are used directly, r

Wind speed at 10m used directly without height correction; ERA5 and most reanalysis products provide wind at 10m height. COSIPY expects U2 at 2m (the measurement height z=2.0 in constants.toml). cadence_evidence.value: Closure is mass-balance for snow water, soil moisture, surface water, groundwater and routed streamflow within each HRU and across HRU linkages. Energy-balance closure is enforced inside the snow modules (SnobalCRHM, ebsm) but is not extended to a fully closed surface energy budget for the whole HRU. Hourly forcing is preferred; daily timesteps are supported but down-sample diurnal cycles. A small (~4-5%) un-closable residual in decadal runs is a known artefact of Netroute lag-storage stores (hruDelay, ssrDelay, runDelay, gwDelay, Kstorage/Lag) which lack declvar outputs.

cadence_evidence.value: Gridded distributed model (0.5 deg / 5 arcmin / 1 km) with kinematic-wave stream routing on a local-drain-direction network; sub-grid heterogeneity via up to 10 DEM elevation zones and six fractional land-cover classes, real cell flux = fraction-weighted sum. Mass-balance closure applies to water (DeltaS = P - ET - Q_out + Q_in, closes to within ~1% over multi-year periods). River routing advances on sub-daily substeps internally while most processes and I/O are daily. No surface energy-balance closure: PET is a demand-side Penman-Monteith/Priestley-Taylor flux, not a closed energy budget.

KSat units wrong — CWatM expects cm/day, input may be mm/hr or m/s; CWatM reads KSat in cm/day. SoilGrids provides mm/hr (factor 2.4 to cm/day). Some datasets provide m/s (factor 8,640,000 to cm/day). Using mm/hr values directly (without ×2.4) makes KSat ~2.4× too low. Using m/s values without conve

Convert KSat to cm/day before use; convert_soil_to_cwatm; ['HWSD: already cm/day (no conversion)', 'SoilGrids: cm/day = mm/hr × 2.4', 'm/s: cm/day = m/s × 8640000', 'Typical range: Sand 100-700, Loam 5-50, Clay 0.5-5 cm/day']; validate_outputs() checks KSat range

Convert ArcGIS D8 to PCRaster LDD convention; ['ArcGIS mapping: 1→6, 2→3, 4→2, 8→1, 16→4, 32→7, 64→8, 128→9', 'Or use HydroSHEDS flow direction with proper conversion', 'Verify: pit cells (value=5) should be at basin outlet only']; Validate LDD with upstream area calculation

Two independent defects: (1) convert_forcing_to_cwatm used to emit the forcing at its NATIVE resolution (0.1 deg for CMFD) while the static maps are 0.25/0.5 deg; (2) the time filter compared full datetimes, and CMFD daily timestamps are not at midnight, so the final day of --end_date was silently d

The reader globbed every CMFD file for a variable (74 yearly files, or 888 monthly files for the 3-hourly archive) and opened each one just to read its `time` axis.; The year is in the file NAME. Prefilter on a (19|20)\d{2} regex -- anchored so the product-version stem V0200 is not misread as a year

fields.name: river channel storage

cadence_evidence.value: Water storage (river + floodplain) is the only prognostic state; water level, flooded area, and inundation depth are diagnosed from storage via sub-grid floodplain topography. Mass is conserved by a water balance of upstream inflow, downstream outflow, and runoff forcing. The outer time step (default 86400 s) is sub-divided internally by CFL-limited adaptive sub-stepping. There is no energy budget; the local-inertial momentum equation is a simplified shallow-water (not full energy) closure. Spatial discretization is the 15-arcmin (~0.25 deg) unit-catchment river network in the HydroCraft regional binding, cut from the global MERIT-Hydro-based glb_15min map; the model itself supports 15/6/5/3/1-arcmin maps with diagnostic downscaling to ~90 m.

fields.name: wind speed (WS)
fields.notes: ROS scales approximately linearly with wind speed; wind also sets ellipse eccentricity. Expected in km/h; m/s input is ~3.6x too low.

fields.name: wind direction (WD)
fields.notes: Sets spread direction (head of the ellipse). FROM convention; math (TO) convention reverses spread by 180 degrees.

fields.name: air temperature (TMP)
fields.notes: FBP (--sim C) only; feeds fine-fuel moisture. Kelvin input produces nonsensical FBP indices.

fields.name: relative humidity (RH)
fields.notes: FBP only; fraction (0-1) input drives FFMC/ISI to extreme values.

fields.name: precipitation (APCP)
fields.notes: FBP only; affects moisture codes.

fields.name: Canadian FWI System indices (FFMC, DMC, DC, ISI, BUI, FWI)
fields.notes: FBP (--sim C) only. Cell2Fire does NOT compute these; they must be derived externally via CFFDRS equations and supplied per weather row. Missing indices crash or silently default.

fields.name: per-cell fuel type
fields.notes: Selects fire-behavior parameters via a lookup table. S&B codes 0,91-99 (non-burnable) and 101-204; FBP codes 1-20. Codes 0 and 91-99 act as non-burnable firebreaks.

fields.name: fuel lookup table
fields.notes: Maps integer fuel codes to descriptive fuel type / behavior parameters.

fields.name: per-fueltype FBP coefficients (p1,p2,p3,q,bui0,cfl,cbh,fmc)
fields.notes: The 18-fueltype FBP coefficient table is baked into the binary, NOT read from input files. Spain/Kitral/Portugal models similarly carry built-in coefficient initializers selected by --scenario.

fields.model_input_format: slope.asc/.tif (optional; can be derived from elevation)
fields.name: slope
fields.notes: Enters a polynomial slope-on-spread correction. Percent-rise input is ~2x too large.

fields.name: slope aspect (saz)
fields.notes: Sets upslope direction for the directional slope effect.

fields.name: elevation
fields.notes: Used for slope derivation and (in FBP) foliar moisture content. Feet input exaggerates derived slope ~3.28x.

fields.name: crown base height (cbh)
fields.notes: Crown-fire initiation. Optional unless --cros set with S&B.

fields.name: crown bulk density (cbd)
fields.notes: Active crown spread threshold. lb/ft3 input is ~16x too low.

fields.name: crown closure fraction (ccf) / foliar canopy cover (fcc)
fields.notes: Canopy descriptors for crown fire.

fields.name: curing percentage (cur)
fields.notes: Grass-fuel curing multiplier in FBP.

fields.model_input_format: CLI flags; defaults HFactor/FFactor/BFactor/EFactor=1.0, ROS10Factor=3.34, CBDFactor/CCFFactor=0.0
fields.name: ROS adjustment / ellipse factors (HFactor/FFactor/BFactor/EFactor, ROS10Factor, CBDFactor/CCFFactor)
fields.notes: Head/flank/back/eccentricity ROS multipliers (the calibration levers of Carrasco et al. 2019). Default 1.0 = untuned. ROS10Factor=3.34 is a Spain/Kitral ROS-at-10min magic scaling constant.

fields.model_input_format: Ignitions.csv (1-based, row-major from top-left) or random sampling
fields.name: ignition point(s)
fields.notes: Fixed cells or sampled per simulation; can be weighted by probabilityMap. Ignition on a non-burnable cell yields zero burned cells.

fields.model_input_format: derived from fuels grid (Available / Non-Fuel from non-burnable codes)
fields.name: initial cell states
fields.notes: All burnable cells start Available; non-burnable codes start Non-Fuel.

fields.name: ignition probability map
fields.notes: Spatial distribution from which random ignition cells are sampled.

fields.name: fire-behavior model selector (--sim {S,C,K,P})
fields.notes: Selects Scott&Burgan / Canadian FBP / Kitral / Portugal. Must match the fuel-code scheme; mixing FBP codes with the S&B model gives wrong behavior.

fields.name: ensemble / stochastic controls (--nsims, --seed, --weather {rows,random}, ROS-CV)
fields.notes: Number of Monte Carlo simulations, RNG seed, deterministic vs randomized weather selection, and the ROS coefficient-of-variation perturbation level driving probabilistic scars.

fields.name: time-stepping controls (--Weather-Period-Length, --Fire-Period-Length, --max-fire-periods)
fields.notes: Fire-Period-Length silently clamped to Weather-Period-Length if larger; too-large fire period skips cells (checkerboard scars).

fields.notes: ROS-Threshold is the per-cell ignition floor. --cros enables crown fire. --fmc is S&B foliar moisture; low values inflate crown fire. --scenario (1-3) sets S&B fire-weather severity and can shift burned area ~10x.

cadence_evidence.value: Cellular-automaton landscape model with no conserved mass/energy budget; cells evolve through discrete burn states over fire periods. Fire propagates center-to-center between 8-connected cells; a receiver cell ignites when the incoming elliptically-allocated ROS exceeds the ROS-Threshold (default 0.1 m/min). Event duration is bounded by available fuel (available cells remaining), weather-record length, and the optional --max-fire-periods horizon. Weather is uniform across the grid (single station, hourly). The fire period length is silently clamped to the weather period length if larger.

cadence_evidence.value: This is a forcing-generation and ensemble-orchestration framework, not a balance-closing physical model. Delta-change is a stateless transform: only monthly means of temperature (additive) and precipitation (multiplicative) are altered; the remaining four of seven VIC forcing variables (wind, pressure, shortwave/longwave radiation, humidity) pass through from the baseline. Mass/energy closure is a property of the downstream VIC model. The China bias-corrected path is mainland-China-only (73.75-135.25E, 15.25-53.75N, 0.25 deg, 4163 land cells); the NEX-GDDP path is global at 0.25 deg.

fields.model_input_format: obs_seq ASCII or binary file: header (copies, QC fields, count) + per-obs {location, time (days,seconds), obs type, error variance, value, QC}
fields.name: observation sequence (obs_seq)
fields.notes: Consumed per assimilation window. Error field stores VARIANCE (sigma^2), NOT standard deviation. Missing-value sentinel is exactly -888888.0 (a valid float, never NaN).

fields.name: cutoff
fields.notes: Gaspari-Cohn localization half-width; observations beyond 2x cutoff have zero impact. Hardcoded default 0.2.

fields.name: inflation parameters (inf_initial, inf_damping, inf_lower_bound, inf_upper_bound, inf_sd_*)
fields.notes: Multiplicative covariance inflation magnitude/persistence. Defaults: inf_initial=1.0 (none), inf_damping=1.0 (no damping), inf_upper_bound=1e6 (effectively unbounded), inf_sd_max_change=1.05.

fields.name: ens_size
fields.notes: Number of ensemble members (20-1000 typical); trades sampling error against cost and keys the sampling-error-correction table. Default 20.

fields.name: perturbation_amplitude
fields.notes: Stddev of Gaussian perturbation when building an ensemble from a single state (perturb_from_single_instance). Default 0.2; near-machine-epsilon values give zero spread.

fields.name: outlier_threshold / input_qc_threshold
fields.notes: outlier_threshold default -1 (disabled); positive N rejects obs with |obs - prior_mean| > N*sqrt(spread^2 + obs_err^2). input_qc_threshold default 3.0 rejects high incoming QC.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF filter_input*.nc (input_state_file_list, or single_file_in with an ens dimension)
fields.name: ensemble state files
fields.notes: Ensemble of host-model restart states at cycle start; dimensionality and variables set by the host model. ens_size must match the available member count.

fields.name: inflation restart fields
fields.notes: Adaptive inflation mean/sd fields carried across cycles; required when inf_initial_from_restart=.true. Persistence governed by inf_damping.

fields.name: model-advance mode (async)
fields.notes: 0 = synchronous in-binary adv_1step (built-in models e.g. Lorenz); 2 = shell command adv_ens_command; 4 = parallel shell launching concurrent advances (external models e.g. WRF, CAM).

fields.model_input_format: algorithm_info QCEFF table; filter_kind codes (EAKF=1, ENKF=2, KERNEL=3, OBS_PARTICLE=4, UNBOUNDED_RHF=8, GAMMA=11, BOUNDED_NORMAL_RHF=101, KDE=102)
fields.name: filter algorithm (filter_kind / QCEFF table)
fields.notes: EAKF is the default per-obs increment kernel; QCEFF assigns per-quantity distributions/bounds to relax the Gaussian assumption for variables like precipitation and snow depth.

fields.name: localization function (select_localization)
fields.notes: 1 = Gaspari-Cohn 5th-order (default, recommended); Boxcar and Ramped Boxcar also available.

fields.name: stages_to_write
fields.notes: Selects which NetCDF state stages are emitted. Default writes only the final 'output' stage; preassim/analysis diagnostics are suppressed unless listed.

fields.name: assimilate_these_obs_types / evaluate_these_obs_types
fields.notes: Types in the evaluate-only list get DART_qc=5 (forward operator computed but not assimilated).

cadence_evidence.value: Spatial geometry and units are inherited from the coupled host model (location modules: oned 1-D idealized, threed_sphere, threed_cartesian); DART's own spatial parameter is the Gaspari-Cohn localization half-width (radians for threed_sphere). Temporal cadence is cycled assimilation windows (observations carry (days, seconds) stamps); the host model advances the ensemble between cycles via async=0 in-binary, async=2 shell, or async=4 parallel-shell. `closure: none` because the prior->posterior step is an ensemble Bayesian (Kalman) update, not a physical mass- or energy-balance closure.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure couples reservoir water storage (elevation-area-volume curve) to breach + spillway outflow, and a non-equilibrium total-load sediment mass balance to breach-geometry evolution. Breach hydraulics use weir/orifice/Keulegan relations and Manning roughness rather than a closed momentum/energy budget; there is no surface-energy closure. The reservoir is lumped (0-D storage), not spatially routed.

cadence_evidence.value: Maintains annual plant-soil mass budgets for carbon, nitrogen, and water at a single point. 1-D soil column simulated to a fixed 2 m (200 cm) depth in up to 10 layers (DNDCv.CAN 9.6.0; the parent DNDC95 v9.5 guide describes a 0-50 cm profile). ET options include an internal Penman-Monteith path when radiation/wind/humidity are supplied; this is a demand-side flux estimate, not a closed surface energy budget. Anaerobic-balloon scheme partitions each layer into aerobic (nitrification) and anaerobic (denitrification) fractions from predicted Eh.

cadence_evidence.value: Coupled mass balances for water, heat, solute (inorganic N and pesticides), and multi-pool organic C/N; the organic-matter model is an integral part of the nitrogen balance. Largest internal timestep is one hour; minimum driving-data resolution is daily, with hourly forcing utilized when richer SVAT options (PMSW, SSOC) are selected. The energy/surface-temperature balance is engaged through the Bioclimate/SVAT path; with SVAT='None' the canopy and soil surface are held at free-air temperature rather than solving a closed surface energy budget. A distributed multi-column / 2-D water-flow mode exists but the canonical configuration is a single 1-D column.

fields.notes: DayCent weather precipitation is in cm/day (NOT mm/day); feeding mm/day silently inflates the water balance ~10x. (.100 monthly PRECIP is cm/month.)

fields.name: solar radiation
fields.notes: Read only when usexdrivers/usexdrvrs is enabled in sitepar.in (DDcentEVI infers from column count). When present, PET uses Penman (1948); otherwise the model computes its own radiation and PET from air temperature (Linacre 1977). 1 langley = 41.84 kJ/m2.

fields.name: relative humidity
fields.notes: Optional extra driver; read only when extra-driver weather option is active. Wind speed (mph) is a further optional driver.

fields.name: fixed decomposition parameters
fields.notes: Biome-common fixed parameters governing organic-matter decomposition; must match rev 491; not normally adjusted between runs.

fields.name: site climate / soil texture / initial SOM parameters
fields.notes: Monthly PRECIP (cm/month), TMN2M/TMX2M (degC); sitlat/sitlng (decimal deg, +N/+E); sand/silt/clay (fraction 0-1); bulkd (g/cm3); nlayer/nlaypg, drain, basef, stormf, ph; epnfa/epnfs atmospheric N inputs; initial SOM pool sizes som1ci/som2ci/som3ci, strucc, metabc.

fields.name: soil hydraulic / texture profile by layer

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure applies to water (snowpack, interception, evaporation, transpiration, runoff, baseflow, leaching; sum of losses bounded by daily PET) and to C/N/P/S through litter and inorganic/organic soil pools. Ammonium and CH4 oxidation are resolved only for the top 15 cm; SOM only for the top 20 cm.

source_evidence.value: Temperature columns 5/6 of the .wth file are in Kelvin (CMFD raw).
Bypass the heuristic: pre-divide your inputs to cm/day yourself, or use a forcing source whose units are unambiguous (NASA POWER returns mm/day reliably).

The host firewall or proxy blocks outbound TLS to power.larc.nasa.gov. NASA POWER is unreachable from this environment even though other hosts (google.com) respond. This is an environmental constraint, not a KI bug, and cannot be fixed by retrying.
Do not retry. Switch to --source fluxnet for FLUXNET tower tasks (works offline from the site's FULLSET_DD.csv) or --source cmfd for Chinese sites. NASA POWER is not a viable fallback on this host.
convert_forcing_to_daycent.py --source mswx fails with FileNotFoundError inside KISSPATH_ROOT/.../Data_forcing_03hr_010deg/P/P_YYYY.nc.
MSWX default path was mis-set to the CMFD root, and MSWX is not actually deployed on this host. --source mswx pointed at CMFD files and inherited the CMFD layout expectations.
If MSWX is truly needed, set --forcing-dir /path/to/mswx explicitly. For most tasks, use --source fluxnet (FLUXNET CSV) or --source cmfd (if the site is inside China).
convert_forcing_to_daycent.py --source cmfd fails or returns empty arrays for a non-China latitude/longitude (e.g. DE-Tha 50.96N 13.57E, Wooster 40.78N 81.93W).

CMFD covers the China domain only (~70E-140E, ~15N-55N). Querying it outside this window either returns no grid cell or raises FileNotFoundError on per-year NetCDFs. validate_inputs now hard-refuses CMFD for lon outside 70-140E.

HWSD returns OC as percent (e.g., 0.86% = 0.86). The old threshold (> 1.5) missed typical values 0.5-1.5 which were written directly as OM fraction instead of being divided by 100. A value of 0.86 in the fraction column means 86% organic matter (peat), not 0.86% OC.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass/volume balance is the kernel's conserved quantity: continuity is solved implicitly (theta-method) for water level s1 across the whole domain in one combined system, with a diagnostic volume-error accumulator (volerr/volerrcum). Scalar transport conserves constituent mass under advection-diffusion. Surface heat exchange is a demand-side flux into the temperature equation, not a closed surface energy budget. Spatial discretization is a finite-volume staggered unstructured mesh (cells: triangles/quads/pentagons/hexagons or curvilinear) with sigma, z, or z-sigma vertical layering; projected (metric) coordinates are required for correct areas/volumes.

cadence_evidence.value: Time integration is an implicit (backward) Euler time loop with adaptive Newton-driven timestepping; the enum bucket sub-hourly reflects that the adaptive step ranges from sub-second to large, not a fixed grain. All time parameters are SI seconds (DtInitial typically ~1% of TEnd); the documented HydroCraft groundwater case can be run steady-state or transient. Closure is per-phase / per-component mass conservation discretized by finite volume (cell-centered TPFA/MPFA or vertex-centered box/CVFE). Momentum is given by the multiphase extended Darcy law v_alpha = -(kr_alpha/mu_alpha) K (grad p_alpha - rho_alpha g), not a solved momentum equation, in the porous-medium models. Constitutive closure (capillary pressure pc = p_n - p_w, relative permeability kr(Sw)) reduces unknowns to the chosen primary variables. Spatial extents in meters; pressures absolute (Pa). Non-isothermal closure (energy balance) applies only when a non-isothermal model (e.g. OnePNI) is active; free-flow / poromechanics closures apply only in those optional model families. The HydroCraft groundwater use case documented in the KI is a single-phase (1p) steady-state or transient Darcy application.

cadence_evidence.value: Spatial discretization is the user-defined network graph of nodes (junctions, reservoirs, tanks) and links (pipes, pumps, valves), not a fixed mesh; default hydraulic/pattern/report time step is 3600 s (1 hr), but the actual step is event-limited (shortened by tank fill/empty, control activation, and rule firing). Closure combines conservation of mass (flow continuity at all nodes) and conservation of energy (head loss) solved together via Todini's Global Gradient Algorithm; the "energy" here is mechanical/hydraulic head-loss energy, not a surface or thermal energy budget (see safety.assumptions). Water-quality transport additionally closes a constituent mass balance. Reservoirs act as infinite source/sinks whose head and quality are unaffected by the network; at least one fixed-grade node (reservoir or tank) is required as a boundary condition.

cadence_evidence.value: Single hydrologic land use unit (HLU) homogeneous in climate, soil, land use, and topography, generally field-size up to ~100 ha (erosion equations valid to ~250 km2 sediment yield). Mass-balance closure applies to water and to the N/P/K and C accounting pools (the .OUT BALANCE section reports near-zero PER/DF residuals). The .ANN Q column is surface runoff only, so a naive P-ET-Q closure check on .ANN will show an intentionally non-zero residual (~200-600 mm/yr at humid sites) because deep percolation and lateral flow are excluded from that column. Optional Green & Ampt infiltration resolves rainfall-excess at sub-daily (0.1 h) intervals.

source_evidence.value:
Precipitation in the .DLY file was written in kg m-2 s-1 (CMFD
raw unit) instead of mm/day.

Multiply CMFD prec by 86400 before writing to .DLY. The
convert_forcing_to_epic.py tool does this automatically via
ki_tools_common.load_forcing. Verify .ANN PRCP column is
~500-2000 mm/yr.

Subtract 273.15 from CMFD tmax/tmin before writing. Verify mean
Tmax on DLY lines reads 15-25C, not 280-300.

Solar radiation in .DLY was written in W m-2 (CMFD daily mean
~180) instead of MJ m-2 day-1 (~15).

Use build_soil_file.py with HWSD-derived bulk density (usually
1.35-1.55 t/m3). Verify .SIT row 5 has CN 75-85 for row crops.

HWSD gives organic carbon as g/g. The .SOL format expects
percent (0-100). Writing g/g gives 100x too little; multiplying
twice gives 100x too much.

The CMFD V2.0 archive ships two stores. Data_forcing_01dy_010deg (daily)
contains a daily MEAN temperature only, so ki_tools_common.load_forcing
returns temp_max_c == temp_min_c == temp_mean_c. Data_forcing_03hr_010deg
(3-hourly) is the only store from which a true daily TMX/TMN can be
aggregated. P

cadence_evidence.value: Solves full-Stokes mass + momentum conservation for incompressible ice coupled to free-surface kinematic equations and an energy/temperature balance; the SSA/SIA configurations are depth-integrated asymptotic reductions of the same conservation laws. Energy-balance closure applies through the temperature/enthalpy solver; mass-balance closure is enforced by the ThicknessSolver. The model uses a non-SI MPa-m-a internal unit system rather than raw SI, so coupling values across solvers assume that unit system. The temporal grain is annual for the default SSA ice-sheet configuration (glaciology runs typically step at 1 year = 31556926 s); the marine-terminating calving sub-configuration runs at sub-daily steps (0.25-2 days, i.e. event-to-daily grain), so the annual label reflects the default ice-sheet config rather than the calving config.

fields.model_input_format: DRIV1D=1 space-delimited ASCII met file, no header, one row per timestep (col 5)
fields.name: SW
fields.notes: Incoming shortwave; must be >=0. Treated as all-diffuse unless SWPART=1, which splits diffuse/direct via solar position.

fields.name: LW
fields.notes: Incoming longwave; physical range ~50-600 W m-2.

fields.model_input_format: met file col 7 (DRIV1D=1); cols 7-8 are Rf,Sf order-swapped in DRIV1D=2 ESM-SnowMIP
fields.name: Sf
fields.notes: Snowfall rate; reduced by canopy interception (INTERCEPT modifies Sf inout) before reaching the snowpack when VAI>0.

fields.name: Rf
fields.notes: Rainfall rate. ENSMBL perturbed-driving path re-derives rain/snow split from a Tc rule, overriding the forcing Rf/Sf phase.

fields.name: Ta
fields.notes: Air temperature in Kelvin; physical range 200-330 K.

fields.name: RH
fields.notes: Relative humidity. Converted internally to specific humidity Qa via Magnus formula using Ps; the raw RH is consumed in FSM2_DRIVE and does not reach the physics. DRIV1D=2 reads Qa directly.

fields.name: Ua
fields.notes: Wind speed; floored to a minimum 0.1 m s-1 inside FSM2_DRIVE.

fields.name: Ps
fields.notes: Surface air pressure; physical range ~40000-110000 Pa; used in the RH->Qa conversion.

fields.name: asmn
fields.notes: Minimum (melting) snow albedo, default 0.5.

fields.name: asmx
fields.notes: Maximum (fresh) snow albedo, default 0.85.

fields.name: rhof
fields.notes: Fresh snow density, default 100 (DENSTY=1/2).

fields.name: rfix
fields.notes: Fixed snow density, default 300 (DENSTY=0).

fields.name: rhow
fields.notes: Wind-packed snow density, default 300 (DENSTY=1,2).

fields.name: hfsn
fields.notes: Snow-cover-fraction depth scale, default 0.1.

fields.name: kfix
fields.notes: Fixed snow thermal conductivity, default 0.24 (CONDCT=0).

fields.name: rgr0

cadence_evidence.value: Point / multi-point 1-D vertical column (Nsmax=3 snow layers over Nsoil=4 soil layers, 1-2 canopy layers via CANMOD); multi-point runs are independent columns with no lateral exchange. Surface energy balance is solved iteratively to |error| < 0.01 W m-2 (~4-10 iterations); layer mass and energy are conserved on merge/split and snow liquid water via implicit upwind + Newton-Raphson. Mass-balance closure applies to snow water (Sf - Melt - subl - Roff ~= dSWE) and energy-balance closure to the surface/soil column. ASCII output supports Npnts>1; NetCDF output (PROFNC=1) is restricted to Npnts=1.

source_evidence.value: FSM2 DRIV1D=1 wants column 10 as RELATIVE humidity in percent, but CMFD, MSWX, ERA5 and NASA POWER all publish SPECIFIC humidity. Converting with a generic Magnus/Tetens formula introduces an error, because FSM2_DRIVE.F90 immediately inverts RH back to Qa with its OWN saturation formula (e0 = 611.21
Turbulent fluxes are tiny and the snowpack melts far too slowly when forced by NASA POWER

NASA POWER's WS2M is derived with a fixed surface-roughness assumption and collapses over rough/forested cells — at Sodankyla (67.36N, 26.63E) its 2010 annual mean is 0.51 m/s against 2.30 m/s for WS10M at the same cell. Feeding 0.5 m/s into FSM2 starves the sensible/latent exchange whatever zU says
xarray/netCDF4 raises "OSError: [Errno -101] NetCDF: HDF error" on Snow_cci or MSWX files

conditional_stages.required_evidence: First determine whether this KI/case supports meaningful calibration. If applicable, record parameter bounds, observations, training/holdout split, objective, optimizer budget and independent validation; otherwise document why it is not applicable.

required_stages.required_evidence: Select a reproducible case, KI implementation/mode, period/site/grid and required input roles; resolve metadata conflicts.
Record OS/architecture, installation command, dependency versions and working model/component version.
Record pack ID/version, allowed distribution, complete file manifest, SHA-256 checks and local receipt; keep access details private.
Check actual variables, units, coverage, calendar/cadence, grid/site, gaps, duplicates and input-role bindings.
Deliberately supply missing, malformed or incompatible inputs and confirm the KI fails clearly before accepting a run; retain the negative-test receipts.
Run this KI's pinned loaders/tools and preserve conversion commands, hashes, input/output manifest and prerequisite ordering.
Execute the selected model or framework component using those inputs; retain exit status, log and output manifest.
Check model-specific acceptance criteria, finite outputs and applicable conservation/reference comparisons; do not equate exit zero with validity.
Select an independent site, domain or component case appropriate to this KI; acquire and prepare its own inputs and validate the end-to-end result without substituting reference-case files.
Repeat from the published pack in a clean project and compare the declared reproducibility criteria.

fields.model_input_format: areal flux array (nrow,ncol) per stress period via RCH/RCHA package
fields.name: recharge
fields.notes: Commonly derived as R = P x recharge_fraction; source data typically in mm/day and must be divided by 1000 to model units. Unit mismatch is silent (heads can rise above land surface yet still converge).

fields.model_input_format: head-dependent ET sink via EVT/EVTA package (max rate evtr, extinction depth exdp, ET surface surf, option nevtop)
fields.name: evapotranspiration
fields.notes: Head-dependent sink; source data typically in mm/day and must be converted to model length/time units. FloPy EVT defaults are placeholders (nevtop=3 highest-active-cell, evtr=1e-3 L/T, exdp=1.0 L, surf=0.0); a run left at default ET surf=0.0 / evtr placeholder gives meaningless extraction.

fields.model_input_format: per-stress-period list of [lay,row,col,flux] via WEL package
fields.name: well pumping / injection
fields.notes: Extraction is NEGATIVE, injection POSITIVE in MODFLOW convention. Source rates in L/s (x86.4) or m3/hr (x24) must be converted to m3/day.

fields.model_input_format: NPF (MF6) / LPF-UPW (MF2005) array; hardcoded FloPy default hk=1.0 (placeholder)
fields.name: horizontal hydraulic conductivity (K / hk)
fields.notes: Literature K often in cm/s (x864) or m/s (x86400) to convert to m/day. Default value is an unphysical placeholder; a run left at default produces meaningless heads.

fields.model_input_format: NPF (MF6) / LPF-UPW (MF2005); interpretation depends on layvka; FloPy default vka=1.0
fields.name: vertical hydraulic conductivity / anisotropy (K33 / vka)
fields.notes: Typically 0.01-0.1 x horizontal K.

fields.name: specific storage (Ss / ss)
fields.notes: Typical 1e-6 to 1e-4; governs confined transient storage response.

fields.name: specific yield (Sy / sy)
fields.notes: Typical 0.01-0.35; governs unconfined transient storage response.

fields.name: riverbed / streambed conductance
fields.notes: C = K_bed x L_cell x W / d_bed; K_bed typically 0.01-1 m/day. Using aquifer K or wrong geometry makes the river over/under-connected.

fields.model_input_format: LPF/UPW laytyp (0=confined; >0=convertible/water-table); MF6 NPF icelltype; FloPy default laytyp=0
fields.name: layer type (laytyp / convertible flag)
fields.notes: Default 0 (confined) is a common silent trap; water-table behavior requires convertible layers.

fields.name: starting heads (strt)
fields.notes: Should be above layer bottoms to avoid initial dry cells; default 1.0 everywhere is unphysical for transient/nonlinear runs.

fields.model_input_format: BAS ibound (active/inactive/CHD flags) / MF6 idomain; hnoflo no-flow sentinel
fields.name: active-cell domain (ibound / idomain)
fields.notes: Activates/deactivates cells for the solver; inactive cells carry the hnoflo sentinel (-999.99 FloPy default).

fields.name: initial concentration (transport)
fields.notes: Only for solute/density-transport runs.

fields.name: constant-head boundary (CHD)
fields.notes: Specified-head Dirichlet boundary; too many or too-low CHD cells can drain the model.

fields.name: river / general-head / drain boundary (RIV/GHB/DRN)
fields.notes: Exchange flux = conductance x (boundary head - cell head); stage/datum must match grid elevation datum.

fields.model_input_format: DIS (nlay,nrow,ncol,delr,delc,top,botm) + stress periods (nper,perlen,nstp,tsmult,steady); MF6 splits into DIS+TDIS
fields.name: spatial & temporal discretization (DIS/TDIS)
fields.notes: Steady vs transient flag per period; perlen units must match ITMUNI.

fields.name: unit-system codes (LENUNI / ITMUNI)
fields.notes: MODFLOW is unit-agnostic; all quantities must be in the chosen consistent length/time units. 0=undefined is dangerous.

fields.model_input_format: IMS (MF6) complexity (SIMPLE/MODERATE/COMPLEX), outer/inner_maximum, outer/inner_dvclose; PCG/NWT for MF2005
fields.name: solver configuration (IMS / PCG / NWT / SMS)
fields.notes: Iteration limits, closure criteria, under-relaxation, and Newton formulation determine whether and how the head field converges.

fields.model_input_format: OC package + ipakcb/save_flows flags selecting which timesteps save HEAD/BUDGET
fields.name: output control (OC)
fields.notes: Heads and budget outputs are ABSENT (not zero) if OC is misconfigured; gates the existence of .hds/.cbc.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF landscape layers windU/windV (DIMT,DIMZ,DIMY,DIMX), or trigger[wind;vel=(u,v,w)] constant/time-varying in the .ff script
fields.name: wind field (windU eastward, windV northward)
fields.notes: Primary driver of wind-driven spread; enters the ROS wind factor. Must be m/s; time-varying wind triggers use absolute time from domain start.

fields.model_input_format: Optional NetCDF moisture layer and/or Md/Ml columns in the fuels table
fields.name: fuel moisture (dead Md / live Ml, optional moisture layer)
fields.notes: Raises ignition energy and lowers ROS; spread stops above the moisture of extinction.

fields.model_input_format: Optional NetCDF temperature layer; ambient Ta also a fuels-table column
fields.name: air temperature
fields.notes: Used in the Balbi ignition-energy balance; Kelvin required (Celsius gives negative ignition energy).

fields.model_input_format: altitude variable in landscape NetCDF (DIMT,DIMZ,DIMY,DIMX); from SRTM/Copernicus DEM/LiDAR GeoTIFF reprojected to UTM
fields.name: digital elevation model (altitude)
fields.notes: Topography; internal slope (and aspect) are derived from altitude and drive slope-driven spread. A flat layer yields slope factor = 0.

fields.model_input_format: fuel variable in landscape NetCDF (integer raster); each index selects a row in the fuels table
fields.name: fuel type map (fuel index)
fields.notes: Index 0 should be non-burnable (e=0). Max index in the raster must be < number of fuel rows or an out-of-bounds read occurs.

fields.model_input_format: Semicolon-delimited fuels table, one row per fuel index: Rhod, Rhol, Md, Ml, sd, sl, e, Sigmad, Sigmal, stoch, RhoA, Ta, Tau0, Deltah, DeltaH, Cp, Cpa, Ti, X0, r00, Blai, me
fields.name: fuel combustion parameters (Rothermel/Balbi SI set)
fields.notes: Rothermel/Balbi require SI in the CSV and convert internally to Imperial; do NOT pre-convert. me is a fraction here. Applies to Rothermel and Balbi propagation models.
fields.unit: mixed SI (kg/m3, 1/m, m, kg/m2, J/kg, K)

fields.model_input_format: Semicolon-delimited fuels table: fl1h_tac, fd_ft, SAVcar_ftinv, mdOnDry1h_r, fuelDens_lbft3, H_BTUlb, Dme_pc, totMineral_r, effectMineral_r
fields.name: fuel combustion parameters (RothermelAndrews2018 Imperial set)
fields.notes: RothermelAndrews2018 consumes Imperial fuel parameters directly (no internal conversion of fuel params). Dme_pc is a percentage. Applies to the RothermelAndrews2018 model only.

fields.model_input_format: startFire[loc=(x,y,z);t=T] in UTM, startFire[lonlat=(lon,lat,z);t=T] in degrees, or an explicit FireFront/FireNode node hierarchy
fields.name: ignition points / initial fire front
fields.notes: Seeds the initial front(s); multiple and delayed ignitions are supported. Must lie within the loaded domain bounds and on burnable fuel.
fields.unit: UTM m (or lon/lat degrees), time s

fields.model_input_format: loadData[data.nc;timestamp]; FireDomain[sw=(...);ne=(...)] or inferred from the NetCDF extent
fields.name: loaded landscape state / domain extent
fields.notes: Establishes the domain SW/NE corners and the t=0 landscape fields before ignition.

fields.name: propagationModel
fields.notes: Selects the rate-of-spread model; MUST match the fuels-table unit system. Engine default is Iso (isotropic), not Rothermel/Balbi — omitting it gives trivial constant spread.

fields.name: spatialIncrement
fields.notes: Lagrangian space step used in dt = ds/speed; controls integration accuracy/CFL. Sub-1 m values over large domains create millions of nodes and can hang.

fields.name: perimeterResolution
fields.notes: Target spacing between fire-front nodes (re-meshing resolution).

fields.name: relax (front smoothing / ROS relaxation factor)
fields.notes: Temporal relaxation of node speed: speed = (1-relax)*speed + relax*newSpeed.

fields.name: windReductionFactor
fields.notes: Midflame wind reduction for canopy effects. When < 1.0 Rothermel also switches to the Andrews/Cruz/Rothermel (2013) wind-cap formula Uf=96.81*Ir^(1/3) - an undocumented coupling. Set 0 suppresses wind entirely.

fields.name: propagationSpeedAdjustmentFactor
fields.notes: Global multiplier on computed ROS.

fields.name: minSpeed / minimalPropagativeFrontDepth
fields.notes: Stop thresholds: minimum propagation speed and minimum front depth for continued propagation.

fields.name: time advancement command
fields.notes: Without a step/goTo the simulation stays at t=0 and produces no advancement.

fields.name: dumpMode / output format
fields.notes: Selects serialization format for emitted fronts.

cadence_evidence.value: Lagrangian front-tracking on a 2-D structured NetCDF landscape grid in projected (UTM) coordinates; the fire front is a linked list of FireNode markers advanced by a local rate-of-spread model, while an Eulerian per-cell arrival-time matrix records front passage. Time is event-driven via a prioritized TimeTable (no fixed global timestep); simulation time is seconds from domain start. The engine tracks a propagating front rather than closing a mass or energy budget; heat/vapor/scalar flux fields are produced only when flux models are active for atmosphere coupling.

cadence_evidence.value: Spatial representation is a lumped reservoir / well-field system (single project site, no spatial mesh; gridded behavior only via external TOUGH2/SUTRA coupling). Time discretization is annual by default (configurable Time-steps-per-year, default sub-annual ~4). 'energy-balance' closure refers to reservoir heat extraction / thermal-drawdown energy accounting plus an economic accounting closed over the plant lifetime (default 30 yr); it is NOT a closed surface energy budget — the surface plant uses efficiency/exergy correlations, not a resolved energy-balance solve.

GEOPHIRES is a site techno-economic model, not a weather/time-series-forced model. No external time-varying driver is consumed each timestep; the time-evolving production temperature is a COMPUTED state (thermal drawdown), not an input forcing. (HydroCraft CMFD/MSWX/NASA POWER scaffolding referenced in the KI is wrapper plumbing, not a GEOPHIRES input.)

fields.model_input_format: meteoXXXX.txt CSV column, DD/MM/YYYY hh:mm dates, -9999 nodata
fields.name: AirT
fields.notes: Required. Kelvin input drives energy-balance non-convergence / hanging.

fields.name: Iprec
fields.notes: Accumulated depth per model time step, NOT a rate; wrong rate units scale total precipitation by ~1000x.

fields.name: RelHum
fields.notes: Required. Fraction (0-1) is read as 0.x% (near-zero ET).

fields.name: WindDir
fields.notes: Recommended; drives terrain wind redistribution and blowing snow.

fields.name: Swglobal
fields.notes: Instantaneous incoming shortwave; accumulated J/m2 (e.g. ERA5) must be deaccumulated.

fields.name: LWin
fields.notes: Optional incoming longwave; if absent, parameterized from cloudiness (Konzelmann/Angstrom).

fields.name: CloudTrans
fields.notes: Optional cloud transmissivity; supplying both LWin and CloudTrans double-parameterizes longwave.

fields.name: DewT
fields.notes: Optional dew-point temperature.

fields.name: AirPress
fields.notes: Optional air pressure.

fields.model_input_format: soilXXXX.txt CSV, one row per layer top-to-bottom
fields.name: Dz
fields.notes: Soil layer thickness (range ~10-500 mm); m or cm input collapses sub-mm layers and diverges the Richards solver.

fields.name: Kh
fields.notes: Lateral saturated hydraulic conductivity (1E-7 to 1E-3 m/s).

fields.name: Kv
fields.notes: Vertical (normal) saturated hydraulic conductivity (1E-7 to 1E-3 m/s).

fields.name: vwc_r
fields.notes: Residual water content; must satisfy vwc_r < vwc_w < vwc_fc < vwc_s.

fields.name: vwc_w
fields.notes: Wilting point.

fields.name: vwc_fc
fields.notes: Field capacity.

fields.name: vwc_s
fields.notes: Saturated water content.

fields.name: alpha
fields.notes: Van Genuchten alpha (0.0001-0.01 1/mm); 1/cm input distorts the retention curve by 10x.

fields.name: n
fields.notes: Van Genuchten n (1.1-3.0); n<=1.0 makes m=1-1/n non-positive (FPE).

fields.name: stor
fields.notes: Specific storativity (~5E-7).

fields.name: VegHeight
fields.notes: Canopy height (meadow 300-600, shrub 1000-3000, forest 5000-30000 mm); m input treated as mm (effectively bare ground).

fields.name: LSAI
fields.notes: Leaf+stem area index (0.5-8.0); below LSAIthres (~0.1) canopy is treated as absent.

fields.name: MinStomatalRes
fields.notes: Minimum stomatal resistance controlling transpiration demand.

fields.name: dem.txt
fields.notes: Distributed mode only; all maps must share ncols/nrows/cellsize/origin/NODATA.

fields.name: slope.txt
fields.notes: Percent instead of degrees distorts runoff response.

fields.name: aspect.txt
fields.notes: Radians instead of degrees flattens/reverses radiation pattern.

fields.name: horizonXXXX.txt
fields.notes: Required when FlagSkyViewFactor=1; missing file silently sets horizon angles to 0, over-predicting direct beam.

fields.name: LapseRateTair
fields.notes: Hardcoded default 6.5 C/km applied silently in meteo_distr when no LapseRateFile supplied.

fields.name: LapseRateTdew
fields.notes: Hardcoded default 2.5 C/km dew-point lapse-rate fallback.

fields.name: InitWaterTableDepth
fields.notes: Sets initial soil moisture profile (range 100-5000 mm); high calibration priority.

fields.name: initial soil temperature
fields.notes: Initial soil/rock temperature profile.

fields.name: snow initial state
fields.notes: Initial snowpack state; defaults to no snow.

fields.name: glacier initial conditions
fields.notes: Active only when glacier layers enabled.

fields.name: PointSim
fields.notes: 1 = point/1D column; 0 = distributed/3D catchment. Selects whether DEM/maps are required.

fields.name: InitDate / EndDate
fields.notes: Simulation period; European day-first dates.

fields.name: TimeStep
fields.notes: Nominal step (default 900 s); solver sub-steps adaptively below this on non-convergence.

fields.name: FlagSkyViewFactor

cadence_evidence.value: Couples a mass-balance water budget (Richards equation, snow/glacier SWE, channel routing) with a surface energy budget (radiative + turbulent fluxes, soil/snow heat diffusion). Non-linear water-energy coupling is explicit during soil phase change: the energy balance is solved before the water balance each sub-step so that soil temperature and ice content are current, and soil ice content reduces hydraulic conductivity via frozen-soil impedance. In point mode the 3D Richards solver collapses to a 1D vertical column with prescribed point topography; in distributed mode the full planar+vertical 3D grid is used.
Accumulated depth per model time step, NOT a rate; wrong rate units scale total precipitation by ~1000x.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure applies to water (Richards-equation soil columns, Manning/diffusive-wave surface and channel flow) and to each transported constituent (advection-dispersion-reaction with linear-isotherm sorption). A cumulative mass-balance error output > 1e-6 flags non-closure. ET is computed as a demand-side flux (Penman / Priestley-Taylor / aerodynamic methods), not a closed surface energy budget. Constituent and mass-balance units are user-defined and must be kept consistent across blocks; the solver does not enforce a canonical concentration unit.

fields.model_input_format: met CSV column read per &meteorology; required for rad_mode 0-3
fields.name: ShortWave (incoming shortwave radiation)
fields.notes: Must be clipped to >= 0; un-clipped night-time negatives after interpolation can drive NaN temperatures. Daily values internally disaggregated to an idealized diurnal cycle.

fields.model_input_format: met CSV column; consumed when lw_type=LW_IN / rad_mode=2
fields.name: LongWave (incoming longwave radiation)
fields.notes: lw_type selects handling: LW_IN reads this column, LW_CC computes longwave from cloud cover. Mismatch double-counts longwave and warms summer surface by 3-5 degC.

fields.model_input_format: met CSV column; required for rad_mode 0,1,4 / lw_type=LW_CC
fields.name: Clouds (cloud cover fraction)
RelHum (relative humidity at ~10 m)
fields.notes: Must be percent (0-100), NOT fraction (0-1); a fractional value is read literally (0.7 -> 0.7% RH) and produces runaway evaporation.

fields.name: WindSpeed (at ~10 m)
fields.notes: Outliers (>30 m/s) can destabilize the mixing solver and yield NaN temperatures.

fields.name: Rain (rainfall depth)
fields.notes: Native unit is m/day, NOT mm/day; an mm/day value is 1000x too large and causes continuous overflow. Rain partitioned to snow below snow_threshold.

fields.model_input_format: met CSV column; consumed when snow_sw / snowice active
fields.name: Snow (snowfall depth)

fields.model_input_format: inflow CSV column (daily); one file per configured inflow
fields.name: inflow FLOW (riverine inflow rate)
fields.notes: Inflow inserted at neutral-buoyancy depth set by its density relative to the column.

fields.name: inflow TEMP (inflow water temperature)
fields.notes: Required; a missing/zero TEMP inserts 0 degC water forming an artificial cold density current that disrupts thermal structure.

fields.name: inflow SALT (inflow salinity)
fields.notes: Must be 0 for freshwater lakes; non-zero salinity raises inflow density and inserts the inflow too deep.

fields.model_input_format: extra inflow CSV columns (NIT_nit, NIT_amm, PHS_frp, OGM_*, OXY_oxy, SIL_rsi, PHY_*) when AED2 enabled
fields.name: inflow WQ constituents (AED2)
fields.notes: Absent nutrient columns give zero external loading; AED2 phytoplankton then collapse to near-zero biomass.

fields.model_input_format: outflow CSV column (daily); one column per configured outlet; or internal natural overflow
fields.name: outflow FLOW (withdrawal/release rate)
Kw (light extinction coefficient)
fields.notes: Controls thermocline depth and light penetration; Kw ~ 1.7/Secchi_depth_m. Too high (>3) suppresses stratification; too low (<0.1) gives unrealistic deep heating.

fields.name: coef_wind_stir (wind stirring coefficient)
fields.notes: Sets surface mixed-layer depth; too high prevents stratification in small sheltered lakes.

fields.name: ce, ch, cd (bulk transfer coefficients for latent, sensible, momentum flux)
wind_factor, sw_factor, lw_factor, rain_factor, at_factor, rh_factor (forcing scaling factors)
fields.notes: Multiplicative scalings applied to met forcing variables; wind_factor and sw_factor are dominant temperature calibration levers.

fields.name: hypsographic curve H[] / A[] (depth-area, optionally volume)
fields.notes: H[] and A[] must be monotonically ascending bottom-to-top with A[0]~0 and crest_elev=max(H); >=10-15 points recommended for realistic volume.

fields.name: min_layer_thick / max_layer_thick (h_min / h_max)
fields.notes: Bound the adaptive Lagrangian layer thickness; max_layer_thick too small triggers layer-merge errors/hangs.

fields.name: R_growth (max phytoplankton growth rate)
fields.notes: Sets total phytoplankton biomass level.

fields.name: w_p (phytoplankton sedimentation velocity)
fields.notes: Negative sinks, positive floats.

fields.model_input_format: &init_profiles namelist (depth-value pairs; initial layers equal thickness)
fields.name: initial temperature/salinity depth profiles
fields.notes: lake_depth must not exceed morphometry max depth (max(H)-min(H)).

fields.model_input_format: &init_profiles WQ entries; count must equal num_wq_vars * num_depths
fields.name: initial AED2 WQ depth profiles
rad_mode (radiation mode selector)
fields.notes: Selects required shortwave/longwave/cloud combination; the supplied met columns must be consistent with it.

fields.name: subdaily (sub-daily forcing switch)
fields.notes: subdaily=.true. with 3-hourly forcing produces flat/unrealistic temperatures; use daily forcing with subdaily=.false. unless forcing is hourly.

fields.name: timefmt + start/stop (simulation time configuration)
fields.notes: timefmt=2 for datetime strings, timefmt=3 for integer seconds; mismatch crashes the namelist read.

fields.name: dt_iceon_avg + min_ice_thickness (ice model enablement)
fields.notes: Both must be set to enable the ice model; otherwise ice is silently disabled and surface temperature floors near 0.002 degC. For deep reservoirs (>50 m) dt_iceon_avg <= 0.04.

fields.name: outflow mode (natural overflow / constant / scheduled / balance)
num_inflows / num_outlets (inflow & outlet counts)
fields.notes: num_inflows must match the number of inflow files; a count of 0 with files listed silently ignores all inflow.

fields.name: AED2 module activation list (&aed_models)
fields.notes: Phytoplankton requires oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and organic_matter modules (silica for diatoms) listed before it; missing dependencies crash at init.

cadence_evidence.value: Conserves water mass with an overall basin budget ΔS_total = Δt(Q_in − Q_out) plus per-reservoir budgets; reports overall budget error and percent discrepancy each time step. Spatial coupling: PRMS HRUs (irregular polygons) map to a MODFLOW finite-difference grid through gravity reservoirs (number of subsurface reservoirs equals number of HRUs). The three regions (land surface; streams/lakes; subsurface) are solved iteratively (coupled-regions), not as a single integrated 3-D Richards' equation; no surface energy-balance closure (ET is a demand-side PET calculation, e.g. Jensen-Haise).

cadence_evidence.value: Closure is geometric, not physical: the model solves a universal cokriging interpolation for a scalar potential field whose isosurfaces are geological interfaces. No mass-balance or energy-balance budget is enforced. Coordinates are internally auto-rescaled into a ~unit cube before kriging, so the default kriging range (1.7) is in rescaled space, not physical distance (precision degrades for extents > ~1e6 m).
Static spatial interpolator — no time-varying drivers are consumed per timestep.
Static model; no time-stepping and no initial state to carry forward.

cadence_evidence.value: Finite-volume formulation conserves mass and momentum for the depth-averaged shallow-water system. The bed-slope term -gh∇B is incorporated in a well-balanced f-wave Riemann solver (not a separate source), preserving steady states. Manning friction and Coriolis enter as fractional-step momentum source terms; there is no surface energy-balance closure. Adaptive time stepping is governed by the CFL condition (cfl_desired ~0.75, cfl_max default 1.0). All times are in seconds; lat-lon (coordinate_system=2) uses earth_radius=6367500 m for metric terms, Cartesian (=1) uses meters.

fields.model_input_format: Steady: '.fNN'/'.rNN' Section - Flow Data; Unsteady: '.uNN' boundary time series
fields.name: discharge (upstream inflow hydrograph)
fields.notes: Primary forcing. Steady consumes one discharge per profile; unsteady consumes Q(t). HEC-RAS PRODUCES stage from Q — Q is conserved along the reach for steady flow and must not be treated as a model product. 1 m^3/s = 35.3147 cfs.

fields.model_input_format: '.fNN'/'.uNN' Reach Boundaries section; type code 1 (Known WS) or 4 (Rating Curve)
fields.name: downstream stage or stage hydrograph
fields.notes: Only when downstream BC type is Known Water Surface or Rating Curve; otherwise the downstream condition is parameter-driven (normal depth or critical depth).

fields.name: lateral inflow hydrograph
fields.notes: Optional; supplied at internal cross sections for unsteady runs.

fields.name: precipitation on grid
fields.notes: Optional, 2-D unsteady only. Acts as a surface boundary input; HEC-RAS does NOT compute watershed hydrologic losses internally beyond simple infiltration options.

fields.model_input_format: '.gNN' Sta/Elev blocks per river station; preprocessed into '.gNN.hdf' hydraulic-property tables (conveyance / area-vs-elevation)
fields.name: cross_section_geometry (station/elevation pairs)
fields.notes: Irreducible substrate parameter. Required at locations where discharge, slope, shape, or roughness change; at structures; at levee ends; around junctions.
fields.unit: ft or m (per project unit system)

fields.model_input_format: '.gNN' Type RM Length L Ch R
fields.name: reach_length (LOB / channel / ROB)
fields.notes: Distance between successive cross sections, separately for left-overbank, channel, right-overbank.

fields.name: 2-D computational mesh + underlying terrain
fields.notes: Sub-grid bathymetry — fine-scale terrain integrated as cell properties on a coarser computational grid.

fields.name: manning_n (channel and overbanks)
fields.notes: Identical numerical value in English and SI — NEVER convert. Conveyance K = (1.486/n)·A·R^(2/3) (English) or (1.0/n)·A·R^(2/3) (SI); the unit factor is internal to the solver. Typical channel 0.025–0.05; typical overbank 0.04–0.15; physical range 0.005–0.5.

fields.name: expansion_contraction_coefficients
fields.notes: Default 0.1 contraction / 0.3 expansion for gradual transitions; 0.3 / 0.5 at bridges. Multiplies the |α·V^2/2g − α_prev·V_prev^2/2g| transition-loss term.

fields.name: bridge / culvert / weir / gate coefficients
fields.notes: Discharge coefficients and geometry for hydraulic structures.

fields.name: theta (implicit weighting) and friction-slope averaging method
fields.notes: Theta in [0.6, 1.0] for the implicit box scheme; friction-slope averaging method ∈ {average conveyance (default), average friction slope, geometric mean, harmonic mean}.

fields.name: eddy viscosity / turbulence closure parameters (2-D)
fields.notes: Reynolds-averaged turbulence closure for SWE solver.

fields.model_input_format: '.uNN' initial conditions section; or steady backwater warm-up
fields.name: initial flow at upstream end of each reach (1-D unsteady)
fields.notes: Defines the steady backwater profile used as t=0 state for unsteady routing.

fields.name: initial water-surface profile (restart)
fields.notes: Optional alternative to the warm-up; supplies WS at every cross section at t=0.

fields.name: initial water-surface elevation per 2-D area
fields.notes: Or supplied implicitly by a warm-up period.

fields.name: initial bed elevation and gradation (sediment runs)
fields.notes: Active-layer composition initialised per cross section.
fields.unit: ft or m; fraction by mass

fields.name: upstream BC type code
fields.notes: Selects how the upstream end of the domain is closed.

fields.name: downstream BC type code
fields.notes: Default Normal Depth (Type 3) uses bed slope as energy slope; induces an error band typically ≥ 5 km near the downstream boundary.

fields.name: downstream_boundary_slope (when BC type = Normal Depth)
fields.notes: Slope is dimensionless — never scale across unit systems.

fields.name: flow_regime
fields.notes: Mixed allows hydraulic-jump location; subcritical solves upstream from the downstream BC, supercritical solves downstream from the upstream BC.

fields.name: unit_system
fields.notes: Controls the 1.486 vs 1.0 internal conveyance factor and the expected units of geometry/observed-WS inputs.

fields.name: 2-D solver type (SWE vs DSW)
fields.notes: DSW is faster but valid only when barotropic pressure gradient and bottom friction dominate.

fields.name: gate openings, pump rules, rule-controlled structure states
fields.notes: Time-varying operational decisions for hydraulic structures during unsteady runs.
fields.unit: varies (gate openings in ft or m; rule-time series)

cadence_evidence.value: 1-D Saint-Venant closes mass + momentum with Manning friction; steady 1-D closes the energy (Bernoulli) equation between sections. 2-D SWE closes mass + momentum under incompressible, uniform-density, hydrostatic-pressure assumptions with Reynolds-averaged eddy-viscosity turbulence closure. The diffusion-wave (DSW) variant simplifies momentum by dropping local-inertia and advective acceleration terms; valid only when barotropic pressure gradient and bottom friction dominate. Energy-balance closure (water temperature / latent heat) appears only in the optional water-quality module, not in the hydrodynamic core. Spatial discretization is distributed-stream (1-D cross sections along reaches, per docs_reader spatial_grain) for the 1-D steady/unsteady solvers; 2-D solver overlays a structured/unstructured computational mesh with sub-grid bathymetry on top of the same river-system schematic. The single-enum spatial tag is the 1-D backbone; 2-D is an opt-in mesh extension. Temporal grain spans steady (time-invariant per profile) through sub-hourly unsteady routing (Δt ≤ Δx/√(g·h) Courant-limited) up to multi-day flood events; the 'event' tag reflects the dominant flood-routing use case.

fields.name: Pobs (precipitation)
fields.notes: Mandatory every timestep; no missing/negative values; must cover the full bdate-edate range (no interpolation/fill). Header must be line 1 (no !! comment rows).

fields.model_input_format: Tobs.txt — TAB-separated, per forcing/subbasin ID, daily
fields.name: Tobs (air temperature)
fields.notes: Mandatory every timestep; assumed valid at the subbasin's mean elevation unless lapse-rate adjusted.

fields.name: TMINobs / TMAXobs (daily min/max temperature)
fields.notes: Required by radiation-based PET models (3-5).

fields.name: SWobs (shortwave radiation)
fields.notes: Required by PET models 3-5 (Hargreaves-Samani, Priestley-Taylor, Penman-Monteith).

fields.name: RHobs (relative humidity)
fields.notes: Required by PET model 5 (FAO Penman-Monteith).

fields.name: Uobs (wind speed)
fields.notes: Required by PET model 5 (FAO Penman-Monteith).

fields.name: lp (potential-evap reduction limit)
fields.notes: Default 0.8; limits PET draw as soil moisture declines toward field capacity.

fields.model_input_format: par.txt land-use-dependent (one value per land-use ID)
fields.name: cevp (PET coefficient)
cevpam / cevpph (PET seasonal amplitude / phase)
fields.notes: Impose a seasonal cycle on potential evapotranspiration.

fields.name: wcwp / wcfc / wcep (wilting point / field capacity / effective porosity)
fields.notes: Must satisfy wcwp < wcfc and pore-volume sum (wcwp+wcfc+wcep) < 1; define soil-water retention and runoff thresholds.

fields.name: rivvel (river velocity) / damp (river attenuation)
fields.notes: Set channel translation time (transtime = rivlen/(rivvel*86400)) and attenuation.

fields.name: Nutrient pool / transformation parameters (fastn0, humusn0, denitrlu, denitwr, denitwl, minerfn, sedon, sedpp, soilcoh, soilerod)

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-conservative water balance across subbasins and SLC classes; dedicated wb* water-balance output files audit all flows. Substances are carried as concentrations following each water flux plus immobile soil/sediment pools (N, P, organic C, sediment, tracers, silica), conserving substance mass alongside water. No surface energy-balance closure; PET options 0-5 are demand-side flux formulations (temperature-index for 0-2, radiation-based for 3-4, FAO Penman-Monteith for 5).

cadence_evidence.value: Static, steady-state topographic delineation on an arbitrary polygonal mesh; there is no time integration (the KI 'sDate' is a label only) and no mass/energy conservation budget. Distances, areas, and angles are computed with spherical geometry (great-circle distance, spherical area). Drainage is reported as an unweighted upstream cell COUNT; actual drainage area requires multiplying by per-cell area. 'distributed-stream' captures the mesh-cell, network-topology nature; 'event' is used as the closest single-delineation temporal label since the model has no genuine time step.

fields.name: precipitation (prec)
fields.notes: Internal area-to-discharge conversion (0.01*Area*10000/86400) confirms the model expects cm/day; mm/day, m/day, or kg/m2/s forcing runs silently with magnitude errors.

fields.name: temperature (temp)
fields.notes: Drives Hamon PET (exp(temp/16)) and degree-day snowmelt; a monthly-mean resample of temp also selects the GWLF growing-season CN antecedent-moisture branch. Kelvin input silently saturates PET seasonality.

fields.model_input_format: RainfallRunoff entry in model.yaml; -99 flags for calibration
fields.name: CN2 (SCS runoff curve number)
fields.notes: Range [25,100]; most sensitive GWLF parameter. Internally converted to dry/wet CN1/CN3 and detention DSkt.

fields.name: Res (baseflow recession coefficient)
fields.notes: Range [1e-3,0.5]; sets groundwater discharge Gt=Res*St.

fields.name: Sep (deep seepage fraction)
fields.notes: Range [0,0.5]; deep seepage Dt=Sep*St lost from the basin.

fields.name: Alpha (groundwater discharge / baseflow coefficient)
fields.notes: Range [0,1]. Docs/KI overlap Alpha (baseflow rate) vs Res (recession); both govern shallow-groundwater discharge.

fields.name: Beta (unsaturated-zone percolation coefficient)
fields.notes: Range [0,1].

fields.name: Ur (available soil water capacity)
fields.notes: Range [1,15]; water-stress onset Ks ramps below 0.5*Ur. mm input silently suppresses runoff.

fields.name: Df (degree-day snowmelt coefficient)
fields.notes: Range [0,1]; melt=min(SnowSt, Df*temp) for temp>0. Shared with ABCD.

fields.name: a (runoff/recharge control under unsaturation)
fields.notes: Range [0,1].

fields.name: b (maximum soil water storage)
fields.notes: Range [0,400]; upper limit on ET + soil moisture storage.

fields.name: c (groundwater recharge fraction)
fields.notes: Range [0,1].

fields.name: d (groundwater discharge rate)
fields.notes: Range [0,1].

fields.name: GShape (within-subbasin gamma UH shape)
fields.notes: Range [1,100]. Interacts with GScale → calibrate jointly. Silently set to a single impulse (no in-grid lag) when assigned_Q or InstreamControl is active.

fields.name: GScale (within-subbasin gamma UH scale)
fields.notes: Range [1e-2,150]; clamped to >=0.0001 to avoid divide-by-zero in gamma.cdf.

fields.name: Velo (Saint-Venant wave celerity)
fields.notes: Range [0.5,55]; between-subbasin channel wave velocity.

fields.name: Diff (Saint-Venant diffusivity)
fields.notes: Range [200,4000]; controls hydrograph attenuation.

fields.name: subbasin drainage area (Area)
fields.notes: Used to convert runoff depth (cm) to discharge (cms). km2 or m2 input silently mis-scales discharge.

fields.name: subbasin latitude (Latitude)
fields.notes: Used by Hamon PET solar-declination term.

fields.name: flow length between outlets (FlowLength)
fields.notes: Sets Lohmann travel time/attenuation. km input makes routing ~1000x too fast.

fields.name: S0 (initial shallow saturated soil water, GWLF)
fields.notes: Requires 1-2 yr warm-up to equilibrate.

fields.name: U0 (initial unsaturated soil water, GWLF)
fields.notes: Requires warm-up.

fields.name: SnowS (initial snow storage)
fields.notes: Shared concept for GWLF and ABCD; requires warm-up.

fields.name: XL (initial saturated/lower soil water, ABCD)
fields.notes: ABCD groundwater store initial value.

fields.name: LSM rainfall-runoff scheme selector (GWLF | ABCD | Other)
fields.notes: 'Other' lets the user inject pre-computed subbasin runoff.

There is no surface energy-balance closure — PET is supplied or computed by the temperature/latitude-driven Hamon method, a demand-side flux, not a closed energy budget. cadence_evidence.value: Mass conservation via the depth-integrated thickness equation dH/dt = -div(H v_bar) + Mdot_s - Mdot_b; momentum conservation as Stokes flow with gravity-only body force; internal energy balance in the thermal solve. Operates on unstructured triangular (2-D) or prismatic (3-D extruded) finite-element meshes over projected (meter) domains, NOT a gridded grid; the dimensionality is 2-D or 3-D depending on the chosen flow approximation (SSA is 2-D depth-integrated; HO/FS require a 3-D extruded mesh). Internal time unit is years (all rates per-year); the sea-level equation additionally enforces global mass conservation.
