cadence_evidence.value: Lumped basin-average water mass balance: precipitation is partitioned by Green-Ampt into infiltration and surface excess; soil-moisture storage closes against ET (Hamon) and gravity drainage; routed runoff is conserved through fast and slow reservoirs to outlet discharge. No surface energy-balance closure (PET is Hamon temperature-index, not a closed energy budget). The canonical KINEROS2 solves distributed kinematic-wave continuity at sub-event timesteps; that distributed/energy-resolved physics is collapsed to a 0-D daily conceptualization here, which the KI itself flags as a significant extrapolation when applied to large basins.

source_evidence.value: Precipitation is supplied in kg/m2/s (CMFD raw units) but KINEROS2 expects mm/d. Since 1 kg/m2/s equals 86400 mm/d, feeding raw CMFD values makes a 2.7 mm/d rainfall appear as 0.000031 mm/d, producing essentially zero infiltration excess.
Multiply CMFD precipitation by 86400 to convert from kg/m2/s to mm/d. Verify that daily precipitation values are in the range 0-150 mm/d for typical basins.

Precipitation is supplied as mm/3h sub-daily totals summed incorrectly or used directly as mm/d. CMFD provides 3-hourly accumulations; directly treating each 3-hour value as a daily total effectively multiplies precipitation by 8.
Sum all eight 3-hourly CMFD values within each day to compute the correct daily total in mm/d, rather than using individual 3-hour values as daily inputs.

Temperature is supplied in Kelvin (CMFD/ERA5 raw units) instead of degrees Celsius. The Hamon PET method receives approximately 280 as input temperature, which produces physically impossible evapotranspiration rates.
Subtract 273.15 from CMFD/ERA5 temperature values before passing to KINEROS2. Verify that temperature time series ranges between approximately -30 and +45 degrees Celsius.

Saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ks) is supplied in mm/h (the unit used in HWSD and many soil databases) but the daily KINEROS2 model expects mm/d. A Ks of 10 mm/h should be 240 mm/d; using 10 mm/d makes the Green-Ampt infiltration capacity far too small.

Use one of the exact USDA texture class names in lowercase: sand, loamy sand, sandy loam, loam, silt loam, clay loam, clay. Pass via --texture argument exactly as listed. Check HWSD source data for the correct USDA mapping.
Basin-average precipitation is zero or NaN despite valid CMFD data existing for the region; forcing conversion produces an empty time series

The basin shapefile does not overlap with the CMFD grid, or the shapefile CRS does not match the CMFD coordinate system (EPSG:4326). A CRS mismatch shifts the basin mask to a wrong location, causing the spatial average to fall outside the data domain.

Verify the basin shapefile CRS is EPSG:4326 (WGS84 geographic). Reproject if necessary using geopandas: gdf = gdf.to_crs('EPSG:4326'). Visually confirm overlap by plotting the shapefile extent against the CMFD grid coordinates.

fields.model_input_format: tab-separated climate.txt, one row per day
fields.name: tavg (or tmin/tmax)
fields.notes: Must be Celsius; Kelvin is read silently as Celsius and corrupts all temperature-dependent processes. Precip must be the daily SUM of sub-daily steps.

fields.name: prec
fields.notes: All precipitation treated as snow when air temperature < TLIMIT=0 degC.

fields.name: rh / vpd / press (humidity, vapour pressure deficit, air pressure)
co2
fields.notes: Typically 280-600 ppm historical, up to ~1200 ppm future; with airchemistry endless='yes' a single row repeats for all years.

fields.name: N deposition (nh4_dep, no3_dep)
fields.notes: Must be kgN/ha/yr; g/m2/yr is a factor-of-10 silent inflation of the N budget.

fields.name: texture fractions (clay, sand, silt)
fields.notes: Layer-specific soil type assigned only if clay+sand+silt sums to ~1.0; otherwise a profile-wide soil type is used.

fields.name: bulk density (bd)
fields.notes: Valid 0.5-2.0; zero/negative bd drives negative porosity (1 - bd/2.65) and segfaults. Must represent stone-free bulk soil.

fields.name: soil organic carbon content (corg)
fields.notes: Mass fraction (0.005-0.05 mineral soils), NOT percent; falls back to humus-type/CN-ratio defaults when omitted. Initializes the soil C pool.

fields.name: stone/gravel fraction
fields.notes: Handled internally; soil inputs must be the stone-free bulk soil.

fields.name: saturated hydraulic conductivity (sks)
fields.notes: LDNDC unit is cm/min; mm/hr or m/day left unconverted gives ~600x too-fast drainage.

fields.name: pH
fields.notes: Valid 3.0-10.0; modulates nitrification.

cadence_evidence.value: Each grid cell is partitioned into aggregated land-cover classes (forest, impervious/sealed, water, irrigated, other); ET is computed per class and fluxes are weighted by class fraction before routing. Mass-balance closure on water is checked explicitly via the total water balance residual (twb). Timestep is configuration-dependent: sub-daily (e.g. DtSec=21600, 6-hourly) for flood events or daily (DtSec=86400) for long-term water balance, with channel routing sub-stepped at DtSecChannel; the optional EPIC crop coupling hard-requires daily DtSec=86400. Snow/icemelt and infiltration gating are thermally driven but the model does not close a surface energy budget.

cadence_evidence.value: This dag describes the analytic reimplementation that computes carbon fluxes (GPP, Ra, Rh, Reco, NEE, NPP) diagnostically from daily meteorology and static parameters. No carbon pool is dynamically evolved (C_pool_scale is a static multiplier), so there is no closed daily carbon mass-balance over evolving pools; NEE is a derived identity (Ra + Rh - GPP). The full LPJ-GUESS feature set (C/N coupling, vegetation dynamics, disturbance, century-scale soil C) is documented in the KI but is NOT realized by this implementation and is scoped out.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure applies to the sediment/soil/bedrock columns (topographic__elevation = bedrock__elevation + soil__depth) and to fluvial sediment routing in the ErosionDeposition/SPACE components. The validated workflow this dag describes (slope-area, concavity, steepness, relief, sediment yield at steady state) is landscape evolution: components run on a user-chosen explicit time step in YEARS (e.g. 500 yr/step over 2 Myr) over geologic timescales — hence temporal: annual as the dominant grain. The overland-flow components are a secondary, event-scale capability (seconds-to-hours) with internal adaptive sub-stepping. Landlab performs no internal unit checking, so dimensional consistency across all parameters and the timestep is an external invariant, not a closure the code guarantees. Spatial form is 2-D over a grid (raster/hex/Voronoi/network/icosphere); individual columns behave as 1-D soil/bedrock stacks.
Must be m/s; mm/hr or mm/day inflate discharge by ~3.6e6x. For landscape-evolution runs commonly a uniform runoff_rate.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass conservation is the routing redistribution of upstream runoff+baseflow volume to the gauge: discharge is a linear convolution (per-cell unit-hydrograph + diffusive-wave channel impulse response) weighted by cell drainage fraction and area, so volume is conserved while timing is redistributed. The internal routing timestep is hourly (DT=3600 s, LE=48 hourly impulse steps) but forcing and output are daily; channel routing is the LINEARIZED diffusive-wave equation with constant per-reach velocity/diffusivity, not the full nonlinear Saint-Venant equations. Missing per-cell flux files are silently zero-filled, which can break volume closure low without an error exit.

cadence_evidence.value: Lumped catchment treated as a single 0-D unit (one to eight storages). Water mass-balance is closed by construction; development testing reports closure residuals of order 1E-12 mm, but at runtime the residual is computed and printed, NOT enforced, so solver non-convergence can leak water silently. Fixed time step: daily (delta_t=1 in days) is the validated path; sub-daily is possible but requires delta_t and all unit-hydrograph time bases to be rescaled consistently. No surface energy-balance closure (PET is an external input).

If the raw 3-hourly values are passed directly as daily values, each timestep has ~1/8 of the correct daily total but there are 8x t

Sum 8 consecutive 3-hourly values to get daily total.; convert_forcing.py --format cmfd; ['Load all 8 sub-daily values per day', 'Sum to get daily total: P_daily = sum(P_3h[0:8])', 'Verify mean P is 0.5-15 mm/d for most climates']; convert_forcing.py auto-detects CMFD format and aggregates.

ERA5 precipitation in kg/m2/s not multiplied by 86400.; ERA5 total precipitation (tp) is provided in kg/m2/s (equivalent to mm/s). A typical value is ~5e-5 kg/m2/s which equals ~4.3 mm/d. Without the 86400 multiplier, the model receives ~0.00005 mm/d, producing no runoff.
; ['convert_forcing.py']

Multiply ERA5 tp by 86400 to convert kg/m2/s to mm/d.; convert_forcing.py --format era5; ['Check ERA5 variable units in metadata: should be kg/m2/s or m', 'If kg/m2/s: multiply by 86400', 'If m: multiply by 1000']; convert_forcing.py detects ERA5 magnitude and auto-converts.

Precipitation in m/d not converted to mm/d.; Some GCM outputs and ERA5 monthly products provide precipitation in meters per day. A typical value of 0.003 m/d should be 3 mm/d. Without the 1000x multiplier, the model receives negligible precipitation.
; ['convert_forcing.py']

Temperature in Kelvin not converted to Celsius.; ERA5 temperature (t2m) is in Kelvin (e.g., 273-300 K). Snow/rain partitioning models (HBV, alpine models) use a threshold near 0°C. With Kelvin values, temperature is always far above any threshold, so all precipitation is classified as rain. No error

Subtract 273.15 from Kelvin temperature values.; convert_forcing.py --format era5; ['Check temperature range: if 250-320, likely Kelvin', 'Subtract 273.15 to convert to Celsius', 'Verify: mean temp should be -20 to 35°C for most locations']; convert_forcing.py warns if mean temperature > 100.

Storage parameter in m or cm instead of mm.; MARRMoT storage parameters (Smax, x1, x3) are in mm. HWSD soil depth is in cm; SoilGrids may be in mm. If a 1.5 m soil depth is passed as 1.5 (meters) to Smax, the store holds only 1.5 mm — it fills and overflows immediately. If passed as 1500 mm correctl

Verify source units. Convert cm to mm (*10), m to mm (*1000).; convert_parameters.py; ['Check HWSD/SoilGrids documentation for depth units', 'If cm: multiply by 10', 'If m: multiply by 1000', 'Typical Smax range: 50-2000 mm']; convert_parameters.py documents source unit in output JSON.

cadence_evidence.value: Hydrostatic primitive equations on an Arakawa C-grid; mass/volume continuity is closed (continuity_PPM is positive-definite). Boussinesq (div.v=0) is the default/most-common mode (layer thickness in m); a non-Boussinesq mode (thickness in kg/m^2) is optional. Time integration is split barotropic-baroclinic: explicit baroclinic DT with a sub-cycled barotropic DTBT, and a thermodynamic DT_THERM (typically 1-4x DT). No surface energy-balance closure is solved internally; air-sea heat/freshwater/momentum fluxes are prescribed boundary forcing.

fields.name: subsurface_runoff (QDRAI)

fields.name: wetland_runoff (QGWL, optional)

fields.name: hillslope geometry (hslp, gxr)

fields.name: Manning's roughness (nr, nt, nh)

fields.name: grid topology (ID, dnID, fdir, lat, lon, area, areaTotal, areaTotal2, frac)

fields.name: model state restart

fields.name: simulation.timestep

fields.name: simulation.subcycles / simulation.routing_iterations

fields.name: simulation.output_resolution / output_file_frequency
fields.notes: output_resolution must be an integer multiple of timestep (averaging window); file frequency monthly/yearly avoids one-timestep-per-file output.

fields.name: water_management.enabled
fields.notes: Structural switch turning the reservoir + demand + irrigation system on/off; off gives natural (unregulated) flow.

cadence_evidence.value: Water mass continuity dS/dt = Qin - Qout + R - I is enforced on each of the three routing tiers (hillslope, subnetwork, main channel) and on reservoir storage (floored at zero). fields.model_input_format: LDASIN NetCDF, one file per forcing timestep (YYYYMMDDHH.LDASIN_DOMAIN1)
fields.name: T2D (air temperature at reference height)
fields.notes: Physical valid range [200,340] K; Tetens/Magnus saturation-vapor-pressure terms are evaluated directly on this field.

fields.name: Q2D (specific humidity at reference height)
fields.notes: Specific humidity, NOT relative humidity; typical 0.001-0.025, physical ceiling ~0.04.

fields.name: PSFC (surface pressure)
fields.notes: Sets air density P/(R*T); scales all turbulent fluxes.

fields.name: SWDOWN (downward shortwave radiation)
fields.notes: Model does not internally clip to >=0; negative interpolation artifacts act as an energy sink.

fields.name: RAINRATE (precipitation rate)
fields.notes: Internally partitioned into rain/snow (OPT_SNF); rate units are mm/s, not mm/hr.

fields.name: SMCMAX (porosity / saturated soil moisture)
fields.notes: Per soil-texture class; must satisfy SMCMAX > SMCREF > SMCWLT > 0.

fields.name: DKSAT (saturated hydraulic conductivity)
fields.notes: Controls infiltration vs runoff partitioning; ~1e-7..1e-4 m/s.

fields.name: ISLTYP (soil-type index)
fields.notes: STATSGO/STAS texture; selects the soil-parameter row; 14=Water cells skipped, 15=Bedrock.

fields.name: IVGTYP (vegetation-type index)
fields.notes: Class set depends on MMINLU (USGS 27-class vs MODIFIED_IGBP_MODIS_NOAH 20-class).

fields.name: VEGFRA (green vegetation fraction)
fields.notes: Percent, not 0-1 fraction; driver only divides by 100 when max>1.

fields.name: TMN/TBOT (deep-soil annual-mean temperature, lower BC)
fields.notes: Lower thermal boundary condition held constant at the column base.

fields.name: Soil-layer geometry ZSOIL / DZS (interface depths and thicknesses)
fields.notes: ZSOIL negative downward (e.g. -0.1/-0.4/-1.0/-2.0); DZS positive; NSOIL must equal the count of thickness values.

fields.model_input_format: HRLDAS setup NetCDF 3-D field or restart
fields.name: SMOIS (initial volumetric soil moisture per layer)
fields.notes: Cold-start default ~0.50-0.75*SMCMAX (docs: 60% saturation); must lie between SMCWLT and SMCMAX. 3-5 yr spinup recommended.

fields.model_input_format: HRLDAS setup NetCDF 3-D field or restart
fields.name: TSLB (initial soil temperature per layer)
SNOW / SNOWH (initial SWE and snow depth)
Aquifer storage / water-table (WA, ZWT)
fields.notes: Cold-start default aquifer ~4900 mm (~2.5 m water table).

fields.name: dynamic_veg_option (DVEG)
fields.notes: Vegetation dynamics / LAI source; default 4.

fields.name: canopy_stomatal_resistance_option (OPT_CRS)
fields.notes: Ball-Berry (1) vs Jarvis (2); must be 1 when dynamic vegetation is on.

fields.name: btr_option (OPT_BTR, soil-moisture stress)
fields.notes: Noah / CLM / SSiB stress formulation.

fields.name: surface_runoff_option (OPT_RUN surface)
fields.notes: SIMGM/SIMTOP/Schaake96/BATS/VIC/Xinanjiang; very high sensitivity.

fields.name: surface_drag_option (OPT_SFC)
fields.notes: Monin-Obukhov vs Chen97 exchange coefficient.

fields.name: snow_albedo_option (OPT_ALB)
fields.notes: BATS / CLASS / SNICAR; SNICAR (3) needs optics files.

fields.name: crop_option / irrigation_option / tile_drainage_option / wetland_option
fields.notes: Activate optional crop, irrigation, tile-drainage, wetland modules.

fields.name: MMINLU land-use classification choice
fields.notes: Must match the section used in NoahmpTable.TBL.

fields.name: Time control (noah_timestep, forcing_timestep, output_timestep, NSOIL, khour/kday)
fields.notes: forcing_timestep and output_timestep must be integer multiples of noah_timestep (default 900 s).

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance (water) and energy-balance closure are checked per column each timestep (BalanceWaterInit/Check, BalanceEnergyCheck; legacy ERROR subroutine). Each grid cell is solved as an independent 1-D soil-vegetation-atmosphere column with no lateral exchange between columns; gridded application is a stack of independent columns. Lower thermal boundary (TBOT) is applied at a fixed depth (~8 m); total soil-layer thickness must not exceed 7.5 m.

fields.model_input_format: monthly mean temperature time series at the glacier; downscaled to elevation bands with a fixed lapse rate
fields.name: air temperature
fields.notes: Baseline datasets W5E5 (default, calibration tuned against it), GSWP3, CRU TS4, ERA5. Default temperature lapse rate -6.5 K/km (cfg.PARAMS temp_default_gradient = -0.0065 K/m). CMIP6/ISIMIP3b raw fields may be delivered in Kelvin and must be converted to degC before use.

fields.model_input_format: monthly total precipitation at the glacier; no precipitation gradient applied by default, scaled by the precipitation factor
fields.name: precipitation
fields.notes: Solid/liquid partition by temp_all_solid (default 0 degC) and temp_all_liq (default 2 degC), linearly interpolated.

fields.model_input_format: per-glacier calibrated coefficient stored after mass-balance calibration
fields.name: melt_f (degree-day / temperature-sensitivity melt factor; legacy mu_star)
fields.notes: v1.6 MonthlyTIModel uses melt_f; the v1.1-era equivalent is mu_star (typical 50-600, can reach 0-1000). Pinning at a bound signals climate mismatch.

fields.model_input_format: multiplicative factor applied to climate precipitation
fields.name: prcp_fac (precipitation correction factor)
fields.notes: Default ~2.5; typical 0.5-5.0, higher (2-4) for high-altitude Himalaya/Karakoram due to gauge undercatch.

fields.name: temp_bias (temperature bias adjustment)
fields.notes: Typical -3 to +3 degC, compensates systematic climate biases.

fields.model_input_format: monthly mean air temperature threshold above which melt occurs
fields.name: T_Melt (melt threshold temperature)
fields.notes: Default -1 degC.

fields.model_input_format: deformation parameter for the shallow-ice flow law
fields.name: Glen creep parameter A (f_d = 2A/(n+2), n=3)
fields.notes: Default ~2.4e-24; calibrated against the Farinotti 2019 consensus volume in OGGM v1.4+.

fields.model_input_format: basal sliding coefficient in the velocity law
fields.name: f_s (basal sliding parameter)
fields.notes: Free parameter, zero by default (often ignored initially).

fields.model_input_format: RGI shapefile polygons (RGIId, GLIMSId, Area, Zmin/Zmax/Zmed, Aspect, TermType, Surging, Form); RGI v6.0 default, v7.0 partial
fields.name: glacier outlines (RGI)

fields.model_input_format: raster GeoTIFF clipped to glacier extent plus border
fields.name: digital elevation model (DEM)
fields.notes: SRTM (60S-60N, default), COPDEM (global), NASADEM, AW3D30, DEM3, RAMP. Use COPDEM above 60N where SRTM has voids.

fields.model_input_format: flowline ice-thickness / surface geometry produced by dynamic spinup that evolves forward to match the RGI inventory date
fields.name: spun-up glacier geometry
fields.notes: Spinup default on; if it fails (surging/calving/DEM-outline errors or short history) the run starts from the RGI-date geometry with an initial shock.

fields.model_input_format: bed_h and section thickness from the mass-conservation bed inversion
fields.name: inverted bed topography and initial ice thickness

fields.model_input_format: per-glacier 2000-2020 geodetic MB rate used as the calibration target for melt_f/prcp_fac/temp_bias
fields.name: geodetic mass-balance reference (Hugonnet et al. 2021)
fields.notes: ~1-3% of RGI glaciers lack geodetic MB; regional means or parameter transfer used as fallback. Per-glacier uncertainty ~200-500 mm w.e./yr — avoid overfitting.

fields.model_input_format: consensus thickness/volume used to calibrate the inversion creep parameter A
fields.name: Farinotti 2019 consensus ice thickness

fields.model_input_format: GCM name plus ssp126/245/370/585; delta-method bias-corrected against the baseline climate
fields.name: CMIP6/ISIMIP3b GCM + SSP scenario selection

fields.model_input_format: FluxBased (explicit, CFL-limited) or SemiImplicit (unconditionally stable; v1.6 default)
fields.name: ice-dynamics solver type (model_type)

fields.name: air temperature

cadence_evidence.value: Glacier reduced to representative 1.5D flowline(s); elevation-band flowlines (Δz = 30 m bands) are the v1.6 standard, geometrical-centerline method also available. Volume/mass conservation enforced via ∂S/∂t = w·ṁ − ∇·q (ice-thickness diffusion). The native temporal grain is sub-annual: surface mass balance is computed on a MONTHLY temperature-index step, geometry is integrated with adaptive timesteps (semi-implicit scheme default), and volume/area/length diagnostics are reported ANNUALLY. The 'seasonal' enum value is the closest allowed bucket to this monthly mass-balance timestep — read with the monthly-MB / annual-reporting split documented here. The shallow-ice approximation assumes basal shear stress equals driving stress τ_d = α·ρ·g·h; no surface energy-balance closure (temperature-index, not energy-balance, melt).

fields.name: Inlet velocity
fields.notes: Volumetric discharge Q (m^3/s) is imposed as U = Q/A_inlet at the inlet patch; OpenFOAM consumes velocity, not discharge.

fields.name: Outlet / reference pressure

fields.name: nu (kinematic viscosity)
fields.notes: Kinematic nu = mu/rho, NOT dynamic mu [Pa.s]; water 20C ~1.004e-6, air 20C ~1.516e-5, seawater 15C ~1.19e-6. Sets the Reynolds number / flow regime.

fields.name: sigma (surface tension)
fields.notes: Water-air at 20C = 0.072 N/m. dev incompressibleVoF expects a scalar sigma in phaseProperties (not the legacy ((air water) 0.07) syntax).

fields.name: k-epsilon closure constants (Cmu, C1, C2, sigmak, sigmaEps)
fields.notes: Hardcoded constructor defaults in the kEpsilon model; overridable but undocumented in the wrapper layer.

fields.name: Initial velocity / pressure fields
fields.notes: Vector fields require vector syntax 'uniform (0 0 0)'; a scalar 'uniform 0' for U is a fatal parse error.

fields.name: Initial turbulence fields (k, epsilon, omega)
fields.notes: Must be non-zero/physical: k = 1.5*(U_ref*TI)^2 with TI 0.01-0.10; epsilon = Cmu^0.75*k^1.5/l; omega = k^0.5/(Cmu^0.25*l). Zero values make the closure equations singular.

fields.name: Initial phase fraction alpha.water and hydrostatic p_rgh
fields.notes: alpha.water=1 is water, 0 is air; uniform-0 init gives an all-air domain. p_rgh must be initialised to per-phase hydrostatic values aligned with the free surface, else a large interface imbalance drives spurious velocity spikes.

fields.name: Computational mesh (polyMesh)
fields.notes: blockMeshDict convertToMeters scales ALL vertices; a wrong value silently rescales the domain (e.g. 1000x) and every derived Re / pressure. Patch names must exactly match field-file patches.

cadence_evidence.value: Per-timestep continuity (mass) is enforced by the pressure-Poisson correction (continuityErrors reports sum-local/global/cumulative). The incompressible isothermal path carries no energy-balance closure; momentum closure depends on the selected turbulence model (eddy-viscosity RANS here). deltaT is bounded by the Courant condition (Co = U*dt/dx < 1), so the effective temporal grain is sub-second to seconds, well below hourly. Free-surface mass conservation under the VoF (MULES) variant is only approximate and degrades at large domains.

cadence_evidence.value: Water-balance closure is enforced per grid cell and timestep over the two soil layers (S1, S2), the groundwater linear reservoir (S3), and channel/water-body storage. Hydrology and water use run on a daily step; kinematic-wave channel routing is internally sub-daily. There is no closed surface energy budget — reference potential ET is supplied (or derived via Hamon from temperature) rather than solved from an energy balance. All depth-based quantities are in meters internally.

If the mm-to-m conversion is omitted (divide by 1000), the model receives 1000x too much precipitation.

Temperature in Kelvin instead of Celsius; PCR-GLOBWB expects temperature in degrees Celsius. ERA5 and W5E5 provide temperature in Kelvin (typically 250-310 K). If not converted, the model treats 293 K as 293 deg C, causing zero snow (always above freezing), enormous ET, and numerical instabilities.

cadence_evidence.value: Solves coupled nonlinear mass conservation PDEs (Richards mass balance with Darcy flux) by fully-implicit Newton-Raphson; energy conservation is additionally closed in TH/GENERAL modes. RICHARDS mode is isothermal single-phase (no energy budget). Reactive transport is formulated on total concentration of a chosen primary/basis species set with secondary species from equilibrium mass action. A per-simulation water mass-balance error < ~1% is the operational trust criterion. Default solve is 3-D finite-volume; 1-D vertical columns (NXYZ 1 1 N) are a degenerate case. Works internally in SI (m, s, Pa, m^2, kg); intrinsic permeability (m^2) and liquid pressure (Pa) are the native bases, NOT hydraulic conductivity or head. The numerical scheme is continuous-time transient (adaptive sub-second-to-multi-year Newton timesteps); the KI's operating/validation cadence is daily (FLUXNET daily SWC forcing/targets), which is the value reported in temporal above.

source_evidence.value:
Simulated SWC at alpine meadow or high-altitude grassland sites is
systematically 25–40% BELOW observed throughout the entire simulation.
PBIAS = -25% to -50%. The seasonal dynamics (R ≈ 0.7–0.8) look correct
but the absolute level is far too low. HWSD maps the site as "Loam".

HWSD classifies many Tibetan Plateau, Qinghai, and high-altitude
meadow soils as "Loam" (phi=0.43, Sr=0.078). In reality these soils
are Histosols or organosols with very high organic matter content,
giving porosity phi=0.55–0.65. Using phi=0.43 underestimates water
storage capacity and produces sys

cadence_evidence.value: Default mode is 0-D batch reactors solved to thermodynamic equilibrium; TRANSPORT extends to a 1-D sequence of cells (cell 0 = influent boundary, cells 1..N = domain). Closure is mass-balance on water, elements, and charge: solutions are treated as charge-balanced and charge balance may be enforced on a chosen element or on pH. Equilibrium is assumed for batch reactions unless KINETICS is specified. The aqueous model is ion-association (Debye-Huckel/Davies/B-dot) by default; Pitzer or SIT activity models apply only when the corresponding database is selected.
Time-varying driver only in transport mode; in batch mode there is no per-timestep forcing.

cadence_evidence.value: All major hydrologic processes are fully coupled and solved as a single semi-discrete finite-volume ODE system (3*nelem + nriver states) by CVODE; PDEs are discretized in space then integrated implicitly in time. Mass-balance closure covers surface, unsaturated, groundwater, and channel water and is reported via the optional water-balance output (P ~= ET + Q + dS). Snow (SNEQV) and canopy (CMC) stores are updated by explicit Euler outside the CVODE vector at the ET step, so their conservation uses a coarser timestep. No surface energy-balance closure in the core hydrology build (that appears only in the optional Flux-PIHM Noah LSM path).

cadence_evidence.value: Mass conservation is enforced in geometry evolution and energy is conserved across the ice / subglacial / thermal-bedrock layers (polythermal enthalpy). Closure is conditional on configuration: the default -hydrology null subglacial model is NOT mass-conserving in the map plane (till water above threshold is permanently lost), whereas -hydrology routing is. The snowpack uses an energy-balance formulation internally, but the overall model is not a closed surface energy budget. Internal computation is in US customary units (inches, feet, acres, degrees Fahrenheit, Langleys, cfs).

source_evidence.value: Precipitation in mm/day instead of inches/day — 25.4x too much precipitation; PRMS expects daily precipitation in inches. Global datasets (CMFD, ERA5, MSWX) provide mm/day or mm/timestep. If mm values are fed directly without dividing by 25.4, the basin receives 25.4x more precipitation than reality

fields.notes: Sign convention: positive slope in positive coordinate direction. Min slope ~0.0001 in flat terrain.

fields.name: CLM vegetation maps (IGBP type, LAI/SAI/z0 per PFT)
fields.notes: CLM enabled only. All-barren/water (type 16/17) gives zero ET.

fields.model_input_format: constant, hydrostatic from water-table depth, or PFB file (e.g. global WTD / MODFLOW steady state)
fields.name: initial pressure-head field
fields.notes: Negative = unsaturated suction, positive = saturated, zero = water table. Spinup of 10-100 yr (or less if seeded from steady state) needed to equilibrate; equilibrium when inter-annual water-balance residual < 1% of precipitation. HydroStaticPatch with bottom RefPatch sets pressure at the BOTTOM (surface = Value - total_depth).

fields.name: domain mask / indicator field
fields.notes: Defines basin extent.

fields.name: Overland flow boundary condition (top patch)
fields.notes: Always present at the top; couples surface and subsurface via pressure continuity. Selecting the kinematic vs diffusive overland scheme is set through the top-patch BC TYPE, not a standalone Solver boolean.

fields.model_input_format: FluxConst / DirEquilRefPatch / PressureConst / Dirichlet / Neumann per patch
fields.name: lateral/bottom boundary conditions
fields.notes: Bottom no-flow by default; sides no-flow by default. At least one outflow boundary (e.g. DirEquilRefPatch seepage face) required, otherwise the domain is a closed box with no drainage.

fields.name: Solver mode selection (Richards vs Impes vs Diffusion)
fields.notes: Defaults to Impes (two-phase) if omitted; integrated surface-subsurface hydrology requires Solver=Richards. CLM coupling requires Solver=Richards plus Solver.LSM=CLM (compiled --with-clm; defaults to NOT calling CLM).

fields.name: terrain-following grid + variable-dz (dz_mult / nzList)
fields.notes: With TerrainFollowingGrid=True, dz values are FRACTIONS of total depth summing to 1.0, not absolute thicknesses. dz_mult silently rescales vertical cell thickness in accumulation/flux terms.

fields.name: PhaseSources / KnownSolution
fields.notes: Mandatory volumetric source-term keys; absence aborts the run before computation.

cadence_evidence.value: Surface and subsurface are solved as ONE coupled nonlinear system: the overland kinematic/diffusive wave is assembled into the Richards residual on the top face (free-surface overland BC, pressure continuity at the land surface), not as a separate sequentially-coupled equation. Mass balance tracks subsurface storage, surface ponding storage, overland outflow, and (with CLM) ET. The CLM energy balance, when active, supplies the surface flux but is not itself a closed coupled energy budget of the subsurface. Base timestep typically 1 hr (range 0.01-24 hr); sharp wetting fronts require dt 0.1-0.5 hr.
Unit is m/hr in ParFlow (not m/day MODFLOW, not m/s SI). Use physical matrix Ksat from soil texture, not VIC-calibrated Ksat (includes macropores, 100-500x too high).

cadence_evidence.value: Mixed-dimensional geometry: nd-matrix subdomains, (nd-1) fracture subdomains, lower-dimensional intersections, and codimension-one mortar interfaces. Mass-balance closure holds for fluid mass (and inorganic transport in reactive setups); momentum/energy give a coupled poro-thermo-elastic balance. Spatial grain is 2-D or 3-D depending on the domain; temporal grain is steady (elliptic) OR transient via implicit-Euler time stepping (all times in seconds). Contact mechanics enforces non-penetration and Coulomb friction at fracture interfaces.

source_evidence.value: SMU integer codes in the soil raster absent from the soil-characteristics table (e.g. HWSD v1 vs v2) -> fc4=0, soil-constrained yield zeroed over large areas.
Temperature data is in Kelvin instead of Celsius. CMFD and MSWX store temperature in K. PyAEZ interprets 290 K as 290°C, causing exponential vapor pressure overflow.
Relative humidity is in percentage (0–100) instead of fraction (0–1). CMFD rhum variable is 0–100%. PyAEZ uses RH directly in Penman-Monteith; values >1 produce extreme saturation deficit.
Wind speed is at 10m reference height instead of 2m. CMFD and many reanalysis products provide 10m wind. PyAEZ Penman-Monteith assumes 2m.
Provide spatially varying Sa from HWSD: sim.setSoilWaterParameters(Sa=sa_map, pc=0.5). Typical Sa: sand=60, loam=140, clay=120 mm/m.
Soil mapping unit (SMU) integer codes in the raster do not match the codes in the soil characteristics Excel. Common when HWSD versions differ (v1 vs v2) or when raster was reclassified.
Cross-check: unique values in soil_map raster must all appear in the SMU column of the Excel files. Re-derive soil Excel from the same HWSD version as the raster.
Use realistic values: Sa from HWSD (typically 50–150 mm/m), D appropriate for the crop (0.5–1.5 m). For initial screening, Sa=100, D=1.0 is standard.

fields.name: Length
fields.notes: Domain length parallel to inlet; default 5000 m. Must be in meters (km gives 1000x-too-small domain).

fields.name: Width
fields.notes: Domain width perpendicular to inlet; default 10000 m.

fields.name: dx
fields.notes: Cell face length / grid resolution; default 50 m. Must satisfy 0 < dx < Length and dx < Width.

fields.name: L0_meters
fields.notes: Inlet channel length; default 150 m. Realized inlet length L0 (in cells) is silently capped at L//4.

fields.name: N0_meters
fields.notes: Inlet channel width; default 250 m. Realized N0 (cells) is floored at 3 and capped at W//4; N0_meters/dx >= 3 required.

fields.name: S0
fields.notes: Characteristic dimensionless topset slope; default 0.00015. Enters the stability coefficient gamma = g*S0*dx/u0^2.

fields.name: u0
fields.notes: Reference inlet velocity; default 1.0. Sets Qw0, gamma, and the velocity cap u_max = 2*u0.

fields.name: h0
fields.notes: Reference inlet depth; default 5.0. Sets reference cell volume V0 = h0*dx^2 and dry_depth = min(0.1, 0.1*h0).

fields.name: hb
fields.notes: Basin depth; default null => hb = h0.

fields.name: C0_percent
fields.notes: Inlet sediment concentration as volume percent; default 0.1. Internally C0 = C0_percent/100; authoring as a fraction (0.001) makes supply 100x too low.

fields.name: f_bedload
fields.notes: Fraction of sediment routed as sand/bedload; default 0.5. Natural deltas 0.2-0.7; 0 or 1 gives all-mud or all-sand.

fields.name: Np_water
fields.notes: Number of water parcels routed per timestep; default 2000. Too low -> checkerboard/noisy free surface.

fields.name: Np_sed
fields.notes: Number of sediment parcels per timestep; default 2000. Split f_bedload sand / (1-f_bedload) mud.

fields.name: itermax
fields.notes: Water-routing iterations per timestep; default 3; >=3 for free-surface convergence.

fields.name: theta_water
fields.notes: Depth-weighting exponent in routing weights (R_i = 1/h_i^theta); default 1.0. Higher concentrates flow into deep channels.

fields.name: coeff_theta_sand
fields.notes: Multiplier on theta_water for sand routing; default 2.0.

fields.name: coeff_theta_mud
fields.notes: Multiplier on theta_water for mud routing; default 1.0.

fields.name: beta
fields.notes: Exponent in sand transport capacity q_s_cap = q_s0 (u_loc/u0)^beta (Meyer-Peter & Muller 1948).

fields.name: coeff_U_ero_sand
fields.notes: Velocity-threshold coefficient (x u0) for sand erosion.

fields.name: coeff_U_ero_mud
fields.notes: Velocity-threshold coefficient (x u0) for mud erosion.

fields.name: coeff_U_dep_mud
fields.notes: Velocity-threshold coefficient (x u0) below which mud deposits.

fields.name: alpha
fields.notes: Topographic cross-stream diffusion coefficient (bank erodibility / cross-slope sediment flux).

fields.name: sed_lag
fields.notes: Lambda-style lag weighting on mud deposition.

fields.name: Csmooth / omega_sfc / omega_flow / Nsmooth
fields.notes: Free-surface smoothing and flow under-relaxation coefficients controlling stability of the reconstructed stage and flow fields.

fields.name: stepmax
fields.notes: Max parcel walk steps; when null defaults to 2*(L+W) cells.

fields.name: eta (initial bed)
fields.notes: Initial bed elevation built from S0 topset slope, h0, and basin geometry; not a user-supplied field.

fields.name: H_SL
fields.notes: Initial sea-level elevation; default 0.0. Advances each timestep by SLR*dt.

fields.name: seed
fields.notes: Random seed (numba RNG, not numpy). If unset a random seed is generated and always logged; required for reproducible runs.

fields.name: resume_checkpoint state
fields.notes: Optional restart: restores all grids, counters, H_SL, and RNG state from a prior checkpoint.

fields.name: SLR
fields.notes: Sea-level-rise rate; default 0.0. Must be m/s of model time (convert mm/yr via /1000/(365.25*86400)*If); realistic O(1e-12)-O(1e-9).

fields.name: toggle_subsidence
fields.notes: Enables the radial subsidence sub-system; default false.

fields.name: subsidence_rate
fields.notes: Maximum subsidence rate; default 2e-9. Same unit pitfall as SLR (mm/yr vs m/s).

fields.name: start_subsidence
fields.notes: Model time at which subsidence begins; default 216000 s. Authoring in years starts subsidence immediately.

fields.name: timesteps / target model time
fields.notes: Run length; the run ends when elapsed model time >= requested time, so realized duration may exceed the request.

fields.name: save_dt
fields.notes: Output save interval in seconds of model time; default 86400 (=daily). save_dt=1 yields per-second frames.

fields.name: save_<var>_grids flags
fields.notes: Select which fields are written; with none enabled the NetCDF has coordinates only.

cadence_evidence.value: Each timestep represents one bankfull flood event; the derived timestep dt = dVs / Qs0 (seconds of model time) and real time = model_time / If, with If the intermittency factor applied at config time. No surface energy budget is closed; evaporation is a prescribed demand-side flux.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance/continuity closure: at each timestep an independent LP enforces node mass balance and storage continuity (Inflow = Release + Spill + Evaporation + delta_Storage). Cross-timestep coupling exists only through storage (and virtual-storage) volume; there is no energy budget and no internal hydrology. Spatial grain is the user-defined node graph rather than a fixed grid; spatial: distributed-stream denotes node/edge network topology. Allocation realism is only as good as the user-specified costs and operating rules.

fields.model_input_format: QUINCY-format forcing CSV column SW_IN; converted internally to PPFD via a fixed factor
fields.name: SW_IN (incoming shortwave radiation)
fields.notes: Drives light-limited (Wj) electron transport and canopy assimilation; also sets net radiation for the energy-flux approximation.

fields.name: TA (air temperature at 2 m)
fields.notes: Must be deg C, NOT Kelvin; drives Arrhenius temperature response of Vcmax/Jmax/Rd/Rh and the Gaussian LAI phenology.

fields.model_input_format: QUINCY-format forcing CSV column VPD; used internally in hPa
fields.name: VPD (vapor pressure deficit)
fields.notes: Reduces the Ci/Ca ratio (VPD-linear surrogate in lieu of a Ball-Berry solve), constraining assimilation.

fields.name: PRECIP (precipitation)
fields.notes: Drives the bell-shaped soil-moisture scalar of heterotrophic respiration; not used for a prognostic soil-water balance.

fields.name: CO2 (atmospheric CO2 mole fraction)
fields.notes: Sets ambient CO2 entering the Farquhar Ci computation; must be ppm, not mole fraction.

fields.model_input_format: QUINCY-format forcing CSV column DAYLENGTH (derived from latitude and day-of-year)
fields.name: DAYLENGTH (day fraction driver)
fields.notes: Instantaneous daytime GPP is scaled by daylength/24 to a 24-h mean for comparison against eddy-covariance daily means.

fields.name: vcmax25 (max carboxylation rate at 25C)
fields.notes: Acts only as an upper cap on the N-derived value: effective Vcmax25 = min(vcmax_n_slope*leaf_N, vcmax25). PFT-specific (boreal ENF default 45).

fields.name: jmax_vcmax_ratio (Jmax/Vcmax ratio)
fields.notes: Controls whether RuBP-regeneration (Wj) ever limits assimilation; default 1.9.

fields.name: ea_vcmax (activation energy for Vcmax)
fields.notes: Must be J/mol, not kJ/mol; default 65330.

fields.name: ea_jmax (activation energy for Jmax)
fields.notes: Default 43540.

fields.name: n_leaf_ref (reference leaf nitrogen content)
fields.notes: Must be gN/m2; ENF 1.5-2.5. Sets the N-limited carboxylation capacity.

fields.name: vcmax_n_slope (Vcmax per unit leaf N)
fields.notes: Vcmax25_eff = vcmax_n_slope*leaf_N, capped at vcmax25; the analytic surrogate's realization of QUINCY's N-control on photosynthesis.

fields.name: g1_bb (Ball-Berry slope parameter)
fields.notes: Declared and range-checked but NOT consumed by the assimilation routine in this analytic version; the Ci/Ca effect is realized by a hardcoded VPD-linear surrogate. Documented Ball-Berry conductance is not wired in here.

fields.name: r_growth_frac (growth respiration fraction of NPP)
fields.notes: Growth respiration term r_growth_frac*(GPP-R_maint); default 0.25.

fields.name: ea_rd (activation energy for dark respiration)
fields.notes: Default 46390; must be J/mol.

fields.name: rh_base (base heterotrophic respiration rate at Tref)
fields.notes: Default 1.8.

fields.name: rh_q10 (Q10 temperature sensitivity of Rh)
fields.notes: Default 2.0; >3 inflates Reco and flips NEE to net source.

fields.name: rh_t_ref (reference temperature for Rh)
fields.notes: Default 15.

fields.name: rh_precip_scale (precipitation scaling for moisture response)
fields.notes: Must be positive; default 0.02. Bell-shaped exp(-scale*(P-opt)^2).

fields.name: rh_precip_opt (optimal precipitation for decomposition)
fields.notes: Default 2.5; moisture response peaks here.

fields.name: lai_max (maximum LAI)
fields.notes: Must exceed lai_min or the seasonal GPP cycle vanishes.

fields.name: lai_t_opt (temperature for maximum LAI)
fields.notes: Set near mean growing-season T; if above site T range, LAI stays at lai_min.

fields.name: cn_leaf (leaf C:N ratio)
fields.notes: gC/gN (leaf 30-60); tracked stoichiometrically, not as prognostic pools in this version.

fields.name: cn_root (fine-root C:N ratio)
fields.notes: Typical 40-80.

fields.name: cn_wood (wood C:N ratio)
fields.notes: Typical 200-500.

fields.name: cp_leaf (leaf C:P ratio)
fields.notes: Tracked structurally; P limitation not realized in this analytic version.

fields.name: np_leaf (leaf N:P ratio)
fields.notes: Tracked structurally; P limitation not realized.

cadence_evidence.value: monthly (daily forcing aggregated to monthly; full QUINCY runs half-hourly)

Mass-balance is NOT enforced in the analytic reimplementation: respiration is diagnostic (Ra derived from instantaneous GPP via npp_approx = gpp - r_maint; Rh from a temperature x moisture response), with no explicit C-N-P pools or pool carryover, so annual (GPP-Reco) need not equal cumulative NEE. Energy is not closed: LE is derived from GPP via a fixed water-use efficiency and H is taken as the Rn-LE residual. The upstream QUINCY v1.0 enforces C/N/P mass balance and resolves explicit vegetation/soil pools at a half-hourly step; that closure does not transfer to this surrogate.

Instantaneous daytime GPP is scaled by daylength/24 to a 24-h mean for comparison against eddy-covariance daily means.

The analytic reimplementation carries no explicit prognostic pool state and does not document initial-condition inputs; LAI and effective Vcmax are recomputed diagnostically each timestep from forcing and parameters. (Upstream QUINCY initializes from bare-ground plus a default SOM profile and a multi-decade spin-up; that does not apply to this surrogate.)

source_evidence.value: Temperature forcing from CMFD or MSWX was left in Kelvin instead of being converted to degrees Celsius. QUINCY expects deg C. Arrhenius temperature responses for Vcmax, Jmax, and Rh use (T - Tref) terms. With T ~ 290 K treated as 290 deg C, the exponential activation terms explode, producing astrono

Subtract 273.15 from temperature before writing the forcing CSV. The convert_forcing_to_quincy.py tool handles this automatically when --source is set to CMFD or MSWX. Verify that monthly mean temperature values are in the range -40 to +45 deg C.

Precipitation forcing from CMFD was left in kg/m2/s (raw CMFD unit) instead of being converted to mm/day. QUINCY's bell-shaped moisture response for Rh uses precipitation in mm/day with an optimal value of ~2.5 mm/day. Raw CMFD values (~1e-5 kg/m2/s) are 86400x too small, placing the moisture scalar

Multiply CMFD precipitation by 86400 to convert kg/m2/s to mm/day. For MSWX (mm/3hr), sum 8 sub-daily timesteps to get daily totals. Verify that monthly mean precipitation is ~0.5-10 mm/day for temperate sites.

fields.name: Vlat
fields.notes: Surface+subsurface runoff volume entering each reach per routing period. RAPID internally computes Qlat = Vlat / ZS_TauR; supplying m3/s instead of m3 makes discharge ~ZS_TauR x (e.g. ~10800x) too small (silent). RAPID reads Vlat by position, so the rivid dimension order must match riv_bas_id ordering exactly.
fields.unit: m3 (accumulated volume over ZS_TauR, NOT a rate)

fields.model_input_format: k_file CSV, one value per reach ordered to riv_bas_id
fields.name: k
fields.notes: Muskingum wave travel time (k = length / celerity), typical hundreds to tens of thousands of s (range ~900-360000). Must be seconds not hours; too small relative to dtR drives unstable C1/C2/C3 and KSP divergence.

fields.model_input_format: x_file CSV, one value per reach
fields.name: x
fields.notes: Muskingum attenuation weighting factor in [0, 0.5] (typical 0.1-0.3). x=0 maximizes attenuation; x=0.5 is pure translation. x>0.5 or x as percentage causes negative C3 and oscillating negative discharge.

fields.name: kfac / xfac
fields.notes: Multipliers applied to k and x during calibration (kfac ~0.1-10, xfac ~0.1-5, default 1.0).

fields.model_input_format: CSV: reach_id downstream_id num_upstream up_id_1..n (outlet downstream_id=0, headwater num_upstream=0)
fields.name: rapid_connect
fields.notes: Defines the sparse network connectivity matrix Net (1 where reach j flows into reach i). IS_max_up must equal the actual max upstream count; undersizing overruns array bounds. Circular references cause water to recirculate.

fields.model_input_format: CSV, one ordered reach ID per line
fields.name: riv_bas_id
fields.notes: Ordered list of reaches in the simulated subbasin; fixes the PETSc vector row order for ALL state vectors and must match the Vlat rivid order. IDs must all exist in rapid_connect exactly once or PETSc matrix assembly segfaults.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF Qout(time=1, rivid), read only if BS_opt_Qinit=.true.
fields.name: Qinit
fields.notes: Initial reach discharge for restart. If absent the model cold-starts all reaches at zero flow (ZS_Qout0=0), requiring days-to-weeks spinup; best practice seeds Qinit from a prior warmup Qfinal. Initial volume defaults to a hardcoded ZS_V0=10000 m3 per reach when no Qinit supplied.

fields.name: IS_opt_run
fields.notes: Selects standard routing vs TAO k/x calibration vs Kalman-filter assimilation phases.

fields.model_input_format: namelist integer (1=matrix Muskingum KSP solve, 2=traditional, 3=transboundary, 4=Muskingum operator)
fields.name: IS_opt_routing
fields.notes: Operator mode (4) prunes small matrix entries via ZS_threshold and gives results that differ from the KSP solve (1) by an approximation that is not documented as accuracy-affecting.

fields.model_input_format: namelist reals (e.g. TauM=2592000, dtM=86400, TauR=10800, dtR=900)
fields.name: ZS_TauM / ZS_dtM / ZS_TauR / ZS_dtR
fields.notes: Total duration / output step / routing period (=Vlat step) / routing sub-step. Must satisfy divisibility (TauM mod dtM, TauR mod dtR, TauM mod TauR all 0) and TauM/TauR must equal the Vlat time-step count, or runs read past EOF or produce wrong step counts. dtR must satisfy the Courant/Muskingum stability bound.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF Qobs(time, rivid) + CSV gage ID lists; required when IS_opt_run=2
fields.name: Qobs (+ obs_tot_id / obs_use_id)
fields.notes: Observed gage discharge driving TAO calibration of k,x and the Kalman-filter correction. Must be m3/s (cfs mismatch gives +/-100% PBIAS).

fields.name: Qfor / dam IDs
fields.notes: Optional forced flow at specified reaches and dam-reach lists for the optional non-data-driven reservoir submodel; both off by default.

fields.name: BS_opt_V / BS_opt_Qfinal / BS_opt_Qinit / BS_opt_influence
fields.notes: Switch optional outputs (volume V, restart Qfinal, influence diagnostics) and restart read (Qinit) on/off.

fields.notes: Defines the sparse network connectivity matrix Net (1 where reach j flows into reach i). IS_max_up must equal the actual max upstream count; undersizing overruns array bounds. Circular references cause water to recirculate.

fields.model_input_format: CSV, one ordered reach ID per line
fields.name: riv_bas_id
fields.notes: Ordered list of reaches in the simulated subbasin; fixes the PETSc vector row order for ALL state vectors and must match the Vlat rivid order. IDs must all exist in rapid_connect exactly once or PETSc matrix assembly segfaults.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF Qout(time=1, rivid), read only if BS_opt_Qinit=.true.
fields.name: Qinit
fields.notes: Initial reach discharge for restart. If absent the model cold-starts all reaches at zero flow (ZS_Qout0=0), requiring days-to-weeks spinup; best practice seeds Qinit from a prior warmup Qfinal. Initial volume defaults to a hardcoded ZS_V0=10000 m3 per reach when no Qinit supplied.

fields.name: IS_opt_run
fields.notes: Selects standard routing vs TAO k/x calibration vs Kalman-filter assimilation phases.

fields.model_input_format: namelist integer (1=matrix Muskingum KSP solve, 2=traditional, 3=transboundary, 4=Muskingum operator)
fields.name: IS_opt_routing
fields.notes: Operator mode (4) prunes small matrix entries via ZS_threshold and gives results that differ from the KSP solve (1) by an approximation that is not documented as accuracy-affecting.

fields.model_input_format: namelist reals (e.g. TauM=2592000, dtM=86400, TauR=10800, dtR=900)
fields.name: ZS_TauM / ZS_dtM / ZS_TauR / ZS_dtR
fields.notes: Total duration / output step / routing period (=Vlat step) / routing sub-step. Must satisfy divisibility (TauM mod dtM, TauR mod dtR, TauM mod TauR all 0) and TauM/TauR must equal the Vlat time-step count, or runs read past EOF or produce wrong step counts. dtR must satisfy the Courant/Muskingum stability bound.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF Qobs(time, rivid) + CSV gage ID lists; required when IS_opt_run=2
fields.name: Qobs (+ obs_tot_id / obs_use_id)
fields.notes: Observed gage discharge driving TAO calibration of k,x and the Kalman-filter correction. Must be m3/s (cfs mismatch gives +/-100% PBIAS).

fields.name: Qfor / dam IDs
fields.notes: Optional forced flow at specified reaches and dam-reach lists for the optional non-data-driven reservoir submodel; both off by default.

fields.name: BS_opt_V / BS_opt_Qfinal / BS_opt_Qinit / BS_opt_influence
fields.notes: Switch optional outputs (volume V, restart Qfinal, influence diagnostics) and restart read (Qinit) on/off.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-conserving Muskingum routing: flow accumulates downstream through a sparse network connectivity matrix. The routing sub-step ZS_dtR (e.g. 900 s) is nested inside a forcing/routing period ZS_TauR (e.g. 10800 s) and a main/output step ZS_dtM (e.g. 86400 s); the model is sub-hourly internally even when output is daily. Muskingum assumes a linear storage-flow relationship with per-reach k, x held constant over the run.

Muskingum wave travel time (k = length / celerity), typical hundreds to tens of thousands of s (range ~900-360000). Must be seconds not hours; too small relative to dtR drives unstable C1/C2/C3 and KSP divergence.

fields.model_input_format: .rain ASCII daily series referenced by base-station file
fields.name: rain (precipitation, rain+snow)
fields.notes: MUST be m/day, not mm/day; mm/day silently inflates all water fluxes ~1000x (dt_001).

fields.name: tmax (daily maximum temperature)
fields.notes: Celsius, not Kelvin (dt_003). Day-to-day tmax-tmin range drives MTCLIM/Bristow-Campbell cloud correction; a constant range disables it (dt_020).

fields.name: relative_humidity
fields.notes: Fraction not percent; % input must be divided by 100.

fields.name: Kdown_direct
fields.notes: Must be supplied together with Kdown_diffuse; supplying only one makes RHESSys zero both and recompute clear-sky radiation, causing vegetation collapse in humid climates (dt_019).

fields.model_input_format: base-station daily sequence, paired with Kdown_direct
fields.name: Kdown_diffuse
daytime_rain_duration
fields.notes: If absent, rain_duration defaults to 86400 s (all day) for any precip, zeroing transpiration on every rainy day (dt_022).

fields.name: CO2 / N deposition (NO3, NH4) / atmospheric transmissivity / cloud fraction
fields.notes: Optional atmospheric drivers when corresponding climate sequences are provided.

fields.name: Ksat_0 (surface saturated hydraulic conductivity)
fields.notes: Range 0.001-100; cm/hr input must be x0.24 (dt_005). Very-high calibration sensitivity.

fields.name: m (transmissivity decay parameter)
fields.notes: Range 0.01-20; controls exponential decay of transmissivity with depth (TOPMODEL).

fields.name: porosity_0
fields.notes: Range 0.2-0.7; >1.0 (percent) crashes the model (dt_006).

fields.name: psi_air_entry (air-entry pressure)
fields.notes: Range 0.01-3.0; kPa input must be /9.81 (dt_010).

fields.name: soil_depth
fields.notes: Range 0.5-5.0; cm input gives unrealistically deep soil (dt_004).

fields.name: epc.max_lai
fields.notes: Range 1-12; maximum leaf area index.

fields.name: epc.allocation_flag
fields.notes: Carbon allocation strategy selector.

fields.name: lapse_rate / atm_trans_lapse_rate / dewpoint_lapse_rate
fields.notes: Temperature/transmissivity lapse rates for topographic downscaling.

fields.name: impervious_fraction / irrigation / fertilizer_NO3 / fertilizer_NH4
fields.notes: Land-use management parameters; fertilizer/irrigation only when landuse layer active.

fields.name: sat_deficit / unsat_storage / rz_storage / detention_store
fields.notes: Hydrologic stores reach equilibrium quickly relative to BGC.

fields.name: initial soil/litter/canopy C and N pools (soil_cs.*, litter_cs.*, cs.leafc, cs.frootc, leafn, frootn)
fields.notes: g/m^2 instead of kg/m^2 causes 1000x runaway growth (dt_009). BGC pools require 200-500 yr spin-up to steady state (dt_012).

fields.name: cs.leafc_transfer / cs.leafc_store (leaf expansion budgets)
fields.notes: For deciduous dormant-season start, cs.leafc_transfer (=max_lai/proj_sla) must be set, not only leafc_store, else Year 1 has no leaves.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure applies to water and to carbon/nitrogen pools across the nested World > Basin > Hillslope > Zone > Patch > Stratum hierarchy. Vertical per-patch water balance is computed first, then lateral subsurface routing overwrites patch saturation-deficit state (ordering coupling). Snowpack and canopy energy balances are computed (net radiation, surface heat flux, sublimation), but the daily ET path is a demand-side flux calculation rather than a single closed surface energy budget; energy is not conserved as a global closure term. Hourly timestep is supported but daily is the operational default.

source_evidence.value:
Precipitation input is in mm/day instead of m/day; RHESSys expects precipitation in meters per day (m/day). Most global datasets (ERA5, CMFD, NASA POWER, station data) report precipitation in mm/day. Forgetting to divide by 1000 inflates all water fluxes by 3 orders of magnitude.
; ['climate forcing

Temperature input is in Kelvin instead of Celsius; ERA5 and some reanalysis datasets report temperature in Kelvin. RHESSys expects degrees Celsius. A 293 K input is treated as 293 C, causing catastrophic evaporation.
; ['climate forcing files (.tmax, .tmin)', 'evapotranspiration, snow processes']

Soil depth is in cm instead of m; Most soil databases (HWSD, SoilGrids) report depth in cm. RHESSys expects meters. A 150 cm soil column entered as 150 m creates unrealistically deep soil.
; ['soil definition files (.def)', 'saturation dynamics, water table depth']

Ksat is in cm/hr instead of m/day; HWSD and some databases report Ksat in cm/hr. RHESSys expects m/day. Conversion: m/day = cm/hr * 0.24. Without conversion, a typical Ksat of 10 cm/hr becomes 10 m/day (should be 2.4 m/day).
; ['soil definition files (.def)', 'lateral drainage, vertical infiltration

Use measured tmax/tmin, OR fix by providing Kdown_direct+Kdown_diffuse (dt_019); ['Obtain actual tmax/tmin data (CMFD has both)', 'Alternatively: use split_kdown.py to provide both Kdown components', 'Verify tmax-tmin varies daily before running']; Never construct tmax = tavg + constant_offset for R

cadence_evidence.value: Volume/mass-balance closure on the free surface and tracer (T, S) transport under the Boussinesq approximation; surface energy budget is closed internally only when BULK_FLUXES is active (air-sea fluxes computed from atmospheric state), otherwise prescribed surface fluxes are imposed. Hydrostatic balance replaces the vertical momentum equation. Time stepping is split-explicit: a fast barotropic (2D) mode on dtfast sub-steps and a slow baroclinic (3D) mode on the DT step, coupled at ratio NDTFAST = DT/dtfast; baroclinic DT is typically minutes but barotropic dtfast is sub-minute, so the model resolves sub-hourly dynamics.

source_evidence.value:
Precipitation in mm/day not converted to kg/m²/s; ROMS expects precipitation as kg/m²/s (equivalent to mm/s). ERA5 and many reanalysis products provide mm/day or m/accumulation. Dividing by 86400 is required for mm/day. For mm/hr, divide by 3600. 1 mm water = 1 kg/m² since rho_water ≈ 1000 kg/m³.
;

Shortwave radiation sign convention wrong (upward positive instead of downward); ROMS expects shortwave radiation as positive downward (into the ocean). Some reanalysis products (ERA5 net fluxes) can have mixed sign conventions. Negative shortwave means the ocean is emitting radiation instead of abs

Temperature still in Kelvin, not converted to Celsius; ROMS expects air temperature (Tair) in degrees Celsius. ERA5 and most reanalysis provide temperature in Kelvin. Forgetting to subtract 273.15 produces plausible but wildly wrong values.
; ['Tair', 'sensible_heat_flux', 'latent_heat_flux']

Air pressure in Pa instead of millibar (hPa); ROMS expects surface air pressure (Pair) in millibar (hPa). ERA5 and most reanalysis provide pressure in Pa. Values around 101325 Pa must be divided by 100 to get 1013.25 mb.
; ['Pair', 'sea_level_pressure', 'inverse_barometer']

fields.model_input_format: .met (36-line header then one 10-column row per day)
fields.name: daily meteorology (Tmin, Tmax, wind run, solar radiation, relative humidity, rainfall; optional E-pan, PAR)
fields.notes: No missing-value handler: every day must carry a complete numeric row. cadence_evidence.value: Daily overall time step with sub-daily breakpoint resolution for infiltration and chemical movement. Coupled mass balance (water, C, N, P, pesticide) over the 1-D root-zone profile plus a surface energy / soil-heat balance (de Vries conduction; diurnal energy balance only when the RZ-SHAW snow/freezing path is active). Lateral tile drainage is a pseudo 2-D add-on, not a closed multi-dimensional flow solution.

cadence_evidence.value: Network-routing model on a directed graph (nodes = water-system components, links = flow connections); it is NOT a rainfall-runoff model. Mass-balance closure applies to the basin water balance dS/dt = P + drainage + Q_in - E - infiltration - Q_out, integrated as a continuous-time ODE (QNDF default) with adaptive stepping; default output interval (saveat) is daily (86400 s) but the integration timestep is sub-daily/adaptive. Allocation runs on a separate, typically daily timestep over which flows are assumed constant and the LP coefficients are linearized at timestep start. No surface energy budget is closed.

Coarse computational grid (typ. 50-200 m) carries fine subgrid bathymetry (5-10 m); subgrid mode decouples accuracy from compute-grid size and embeds roughness in subgrid tables. fields.notes: ITMPBC=1 uses a Hirota damping-depth dynamic bottom-node temperature rather than a fixed boundary

fields.notes: JSTART must be first weather DOY + 1 (DAY2HR needs previous-day data)

fields.name: HEIGHT (measurement reference height)
fields.notes: Must exceed maximum canopy height

fields.name: NS (number of soil nodes)
fields.notes: >=11 with fine near-surface spacing recommended to resolve frost penetration

fields.name: TOLER (Newton-Raphson convergence tolerance)
fields.notes: 0.001-0.01 recommended; 0.001 for freeze-thaw

fields.name: PONDMX (max ponding depth)
fields.notes: 0 forces immediate runoff of excess water

fields.name: MWATRXT (external soil source/sink flag)
fields.notes: 1 = external water injection/extraction file required

fields.notes: Select which of up to ~16 output files are written

cadence_evidence.value: Heat and water flux equations for canopy, snow, residue, and soil layers are written in implicit finite-difference form and solved simultaneously and iteratively by a Newton-Raphson scheme to a user-prescribed tolerance. Ground heat flux is computed from the residual of the surface energy balance and must satisfy the heat-flux solution for the residue/soil profile. Mass-balance closure applies to water and to the transported solute species; surface energy-balance closure is intrinsic (not optional). Internally the heat and water systems are assembled as two separate tridiagonal matrices solved per iteration and coupled implicitly through the freeze-thaw liquid/ice repartition. Timestep flag MTSTEP selects hourly (0), daily (1), or custom-interval (2); the solver subdivides each hour into adaptive sub-timesteps.
Valid range approx -60 to 55 degC; hourly when MTSTEP=0, daily extremes when MTSTEP=1
IFLAGSI=0 expects mph (hourly) or miles/day (daily); IFLAGSI=1 expects m/s in both
Same unit regardless of IFLAGSI; daily mode expects average daily W/m2

source_evidence.value: IFLAGSI=0 expects wind in mph (hourly) or miles/day (daily). CMFD/MSWX/NASA POWER provide wind in m/s. Using m/s with IFLAGSI=0 gives ~2.2x wrong wind speed, causing wrong ET and energy balance
Always set IFLAGSI=1 when using CMFD, MSWX, or NASA POWER forcing. IFLAGSI=1 means all SI units: wind in m/s, precipitation in mm.
IFLAGSI=0 expects precipitation in inches. CMFD/MSWX provide mm. Using mm with IFLAGSI=0 gives ~25.4x wrong precipitation
CMFD/MSWX provide period-average W/m2 — this is acceptable for SHAW. NASA POWER hourly provides instantaneous — also fine. For daily mode, provide average daily radiation in W/m2.

Convert: W_m2 = MJ_m2_day * 1e6 / 86400 (= multiply by 11.574). Verify: daily average solar should be 30-300 W/m2 depending on latitude and season. If values are < 10, the MJ→W conversion was likely missed. Note: CMFD/MSWX already provide W/m2 — this only applies to station data that reports MJ/m2/d

fields.name: TA
fields.notes: Air temperature; must be MKSA Kelvin. Drives the surface energy balance and Monin-Obukhov turbulent fluxes.

fields.name: RH
fields.notes: Relative humidity as a 0-1 fraction (not percent); enters latent-heat / sublimation computation.

fields.name: VW
fields.notes: Wind speed; scales turbulent exchange coefficients and drives saltation/erosion and drifting-snow compaction.

fields.name: DW
fields.notes: Wind direction; optional, used by drift bookkeeping.

fields.name: ISWR / RSWR / NET_SW
fields.notes: Shortwave radiation; at least one form required. SW_MODE selects whether incoming, reflected, or both are provided (BOTH derives albedo = RSWR/ISWR).

fields.model_input_format: SMET column ILWR (or TSS as alternative upper-boundary surface temperature)
fields.name: ILWR
fields.notes: Incoming longwave; if absent under FORCING=ATMOS the model assumes zero incoming longwave (severe cold bias).

fields.name: PSUM
fields.notes: Incremental precipitation per timestep (rain+snow); phase split internal. Either PSUM or measured HS must be supplied as the mass driver.

fields.name: HS
fields.notes: Measured snow depth; optional driver/assimilation source for snow-depth-based precipitation correction (do not combine with PSUM correction, double-count risk). NB: the .smet HS forcing is in metres, but the .met HS output column is emitted in centimetres - see safety.conflicts.

fields.name: TSG
fields.notes: Ground/soil surface temperature; lower-boundary forcing alternative to a prescribed geothermal flux.

fields.name: P
fields.notes: Atmospheric pressure; optional, affects vapour pressure and air density.

fields.name: slope angle / azimuth
fields.notes: Station slope and aspect; below Constants::min_slope_angle (3 deg) the site is treated as flat for precip routing.

fields.name: ROUGHNESS_LENGTH
fields.notes: Aerodynamic roughness length entering Monin-Obukhov surface-layer fluxes.

fields.name: HEIGHT_OF_METEO_VALUES / HEIGHT_OF_WIND_VALUE
fields.notes: Must match real sensor install heights or stability extrapolation biases turbulent fluxes.

fields.name: soil layer properties (Rho_S, Conduc_S, HeatCapac_S, Vol_Frac_S)
fields.notes: Soil thermal/hydraulic properties supplied inside the initial profile file.

fields.name: MINIMUM_L_ELEMENT / REDUCE_N_ELEMENTS
fields.notes: Control finite-element layer thickness and merging; too-small values cause zero-thickness layers and ill-conditioned matrices.

fields.model_input_format: .sno data rows (soil bottom-to-top then snow bottom-to-top, 18 fields/row)
fields.name: initial layered stratigraphy
fields.notes: Per-layer Layer_Thick, T, Vol_Frac_I/W/V/S, grain microstructure (rg, rb, dd, sp, mk), mass_hoar, CDot, metamo. Volume fractions per layer must sum to exactly 1.0. ProfileDate must be <= first forcing timestamp.

fields.name: soil temperature and moisture profile (spun-up)
fields.notes: Requires spinup (>= ~2 annual cycles; permafrost 10+ years) to equilibrate before production, or a restart .sno from a prior run.

fields.name: FORCING
fields.notes: ATMOS drives the full surface energy balance from radiation/wind/humidity; MASSBAL uses precipitation+temperature only (use when radiation absent).

fields.name: SW_MODE
fields.notes: Selects which shortwave fields are present and how albedo is obtained.

fields.name: CHANGE_BC
fields.notes: Toggles the surface thermal boundary between Neumann (flux) and Dirichlet (measured TSS).

fields.name: GEO_HEAT
fields.notes: Geothermal/basal heat flux at the column base (alternative to prescribed TSG).

fields.name: VARIANT
fields.notes: Selects climate-regime presets that switch hardcoded new-snow microstructure, RH limits, and bond-strength factors; SEAICE force-enables coupled phase changes.

fields.name: WATERTRANSPORTMODEL_SNOW
fields.notes: Selects the liquid-water percolation scheme; structurally controls meltwater timing and runoff.

fields.name: ALBEDO_PARAMETERIZATION
fields.notes: Selects snow-albedo evolution scheme.

fields.name: ATMOSPHERIC_STABILITY
fields.notes: Turbulence/stability correction scheme for the surface-layer flux computation.

fields.name: CALCULATION_STEP_LENGTH
fields.notes: Read internally as minutes; the explicit/adaptive solver diverges or floods the hazard-interval logic with overly large steps.

cadence_evidence.value: Three-phase porous-medium energy balance (ice / liquid water / water vapour): solar absorption, sublimation/deposition, melt/refreeze, and conduction are closed via the finite-element temperature solve; mass is conserved across precipitation input, phase change, vapour transport, evaporation/sublimation, wind erosion, and basal runoff. Calculation timestep (CALCULATION_STEP_LENGTH) is read internally in MINUTES and the explicit/adaptive solver sub-steps below it; output intervals (TS_DAYS_BETWEEN/PROF_DAYS_BETWEEN) are independent of the calculation timestep.
Incremental precipitation per timestep (rain+snow); phase split internal. Either PSUM or measured HS must be supplied as the mass driver.

fields.name: pptrate
fields.notes: precipitation rate; partitioned to rain/snow by air temperature relative to tempCritRain; temperate mean ~1e-5 to 1e-4 kg/m2/s

fields.name: airtemp
fields.notes: air temperature at measurement height; controls rain/snow phase partition and melt energy

fields.name: SWRadAtm
fields.notes: downward shortwave radiation at upper boundary

fields.name: LWRadAtm
fields.notes: downward longwave radiation at upper boundary

fields.name: windspd
fields.notes: wind speed at measurement height

fields.name: airpres
fields.notes: air pressure at measurement height; expected ~80000-105000 Pa, in kPa breaks saturation-vapour-pressure/energy balance

fields.name: spechum
fields.notes: specific humidity (mass ratio, numerically kg/kg); expected ~0.002-0.015; sets vapour-pressure deficit for ET

fields.name: k_soil (saturated hydraulic conductivity)
fields.notes: range ~1e-7 to 1e-3

fields.name: theta_res (residual water content)
fields.notes: must be < theta_sat; range ~0.01-0.15

fields.name: vGn_alpha (van Genuchten alpha)
fields.notes: matric-head sign convention: SUMMA requires NEGATIVE values (valid ~[-1.0,-0.01]); positive yields NaN

fields.name: critSoilWilting (wilting point)
fields.notes: ET shutoff; must satisfy theta_res < critSoilWilting < critSoilTranspire < fieldCapacity < theta_sat

fields.name: fieldCapacity
fields.notes: theta at -33 kPa; ~0.30

fields.name: heightCanopyTop (canopy height)
fields.notes: controls radiation and roughness; ~0.1-40 m

fields.name: vegTypeIndex / soilTypeIndex / slopeTypeIndex
fields.notes: classification indices selecting Noah-MP VEGPARM/SOILPARM/GENPARM lookup-table defaults unless overridden by trialParams

fields.name: HRU geometry (HRUarea, elevation, tan_slope, contourLength, mHeight, downHRUindex)
fields.notes: local spatial attributes; downHRUindex=0 marks the outlet

fields.name: mLayerTemp (initial soil/snow layer temperature)
fields.notes: cold-start ~ mean annual air temperature; unrealistic values motivate nrg_flux convergence failure / two-phase spinup

fields.name: mLayerVolFracLiq / mLayerVolFracIce (initial layer moisture)
fields.notes: cold-start ~field capacity 0.25-0.35; too dry causes 5+ yr spinup, above theta_sat causes runoff spikes

fields.name: scalarSWE / nSnow (initial snow water equivalent / snow layer count)
fields.notes: typically SWE=0, nSnow=0; snow builds up naturally

fields.name: scalarAquiferStorage (initial aquifer storage)
fields.notes: high initial storage can absorb all water and yield near-zero runoff

fields.name: nSoil / soil layer discretization
fields.notes: default 8 layers to ~4 m; must match model configuration exactly (else dimension-mismatch abort)

fields.name: model decisions (~35 physics-option categories)
fields.notes: selects flux parameterizations and numerics: snowLayers, thCondSnow, snowIncept, compaction, f_Richards, groundwatr, hc_profile, stomResist, soilStress, canopySrad, num_method, fDerivMeth, etc. — these change the structural model, not just parameters

fields.name: bcUpprTdyn / bcUpprSoiH (upper temperature/soil-head boundary)
fields.notes: presTemp/nrg_flux/zeroFlux (energy) and presHead/liq_flux (water); presTemp diagnostic mode bypasses energy balance and yields zero ET hence zero runoff

fields.name: bcLowrTdyn / bcLowrSoiH (lower temperature/soil-head boundary)

cadence_evidence.value: Each HRU is a 1-D vertical column solving coupled energy and mass (water) balance on a common conservation core; the conservation equations are decoupled from the numerical solver. Distributed over GRUs (typically grid cells) subdivided into HRUs, with no lateral moisture exchange between GRUs. The model's operating temporal grain is the forcing data_step, commonly 3600 s (hourly) to 10800 s (3-hourly); the implicit solver adaptively sub-steps WITHIN the data_step (varSubstep), which is a numerical detail, not a sub-hourly forcing grain. Total runoff is emitted as a flux (m/s) per HRU; discharge requires multiplying by HRU area and applying external routing.

cadence_evidence.value: SWAN propagates and conserves the wave action density spectrum N(sigma,theta) over geographic (x,y), frequency (sigma) and direction (theta) space via the action balance equation with source and sink terms (wind generation, dissipation, nonlinear redistribution); it is a spectral action-budget model, not a mass- or energy-balance hydrologic closure. Supports stationary and non-stationary (time-stepping) modes; structured (rectilinear/curvilinear) or unstructured triangular grids; Cartesian or spherical coordinates. A 1-D flume configuration is supported as a degenerate case.

cadence_evidence.value: Daily meteorological driving with an adaptive internal sub-daily timestep (order of seconds during fast processes such as intensive rain showers, runoff and macropore flow, up to 1 day). Richards equation solved with an implicit backward finite-difference scheme and Newton-Raphson iteration ensuring water mass conservation; water and solute balances are reported with explicit balance-error terms, and snowpack and macropore water balances are tracked separately. The default daily Penman-Monteith ET path is a demand-side flux calculation, not a closed surface energy budget.

The QUAL2E channel-water-quality solver (wq_cha=1) is numerically unstable in Rev 59.3 at extreme flows and is recommended OFF; HRU- and basin-level mass balances remain closed in that configuration. cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure on water (and on pollutant mass when water quality is active) is the governing principle: surface runoff is a nonlinear-reservoir mass balance on ponded depth d (dd/dt = i - e - f - q), and node/link/groundwater balances are tracked as separate continuity errors (runoff, flow-routing, groundwater, quality). Separate runoff, routing, and reporting timesteps advance state as X_t = f(X_{t-1}, I_t, P). Mass closure is NOT guaranteed when ALLOW_PONDING=NO and a node floods, since flood water is then removed from the system as a sink.

cadence_evidence.value: discrete time stepping (minutes-per-step set by update_rate)

No conserved physical quantity is balanced. State evolves by a cellular-automaton ignition rule: each burning pixel accumulates burn_amounts (= Rothermel rate of spread x update_rate) until it exceeds pixel_scale, then ignites 4- or 8-connected neighbors; burning pixels are pruned to BURNED after max_fire_duration steps. Internal computation uses US-customary units (ft, lb/ft2, ft/min, BTU/lb) per the Rothermel paper convention, while operational LandFire inputs are metric, creating documented unit-conversion coupling.
RoS is multiplied by update_rate before accruing into burn_amounts, so temporal discretization directly scales effective spread.

source_evidence.value: wind.simple.speed expects mph, not m/s. Writing 10 (intending 10 m/s ≈ 22 mph) produces 10 mph internal.; ERA5, MERRA2, and most weather models report wind in m/s. SimFire's simple.speed YAML is in mph, so writing the m/s value directly (e.g. 10) gets interpreted as 10 mph. This is an underestimate

Derive wind.simple.speed with the NASA POWER mode of the wind tool, which applies the log profile and the WAF.; convert_wind_to_simfire; ['python tools/convert_wind_to_simfire.py --nasa-power --lat LAT --lon LON --date YYYY-MM-DD --fuel-bed-depth-ft H --output-dir DIR', 'Take H from the DOMINANT bur

cadence_evidence.value: Spatial support spans 1-D/2-D/2.5-D/3-D finite-volume meshes (TensorMesh, OcTree/QuadTree TreeMesh, CylindricalMesh, SimplexMesh) depending on method; 3-D is the primary case. Temporal grain is method-dependent: static/steady-state for potential fields and DC, per-frequency for FDEM, time-stepping for TDEM and Richards flow; the inversion itself is an iterative Gauss-Newton outer loop with beta cooling, NOT a wall-clock time integration. 'closure' is `none` in the mass/energy-balance sense: SimPEG discretizes the governing PDEs (Maxwell's equations, Poisson/potential-field equations, Richards equation) on a finite-volume mesh and exposes the forward operator and its derivatives; mass conservation applies only inside the Richards-flow module.
