fields.name: Precipitation (P)
fields.notes: Total rainfall flux. Framework is unit-agnostic; mm/d is the operational convention. Input array order differs by entry element (GR4J InterceptionFilter expects [PET, P]; HBV UnsaturatedReservoir expects [P, PET]) — wrong order silently produces nonsense.

fields.model_input_format: numpy array of length n_timesteps via set_input()
fields.name: Potential evapotranspiration (PET)
fields.notes: Drives interception, production store, and unsaturated/upper-zone reservoir AET demand.

fields.name: Temperature (T)
fields.notes: Consumed only by the Snow Reservoir element; required only when a snow module is present in the assembled structure.

fields.name: x1 (GR4J production-store capacity)
fields.notes: Production store size; partitions precipitation between storage and percolation. Very high calibration sensitivity. KI documents conflicting defaults (SKILL table 50.0 vs tool/example 350.0).

fields.name: x2 (GR4J groundwater exchange coefficient)
fields.notes: Exchange flux magnitude. SuperflexPy sign convention: positive x2 = EXPORT/loss from the catchment (losing stream), negative = import (gaining stream) — per gr4j.py docstring 'Exchange flux (F), positive if loss' (CORRECTED 2026-08-22; this note previously taught the inverted sign).

fields.name: x3 (GR4J routing-store capacity)
fields.notes: Routing store size, controls baseflow depletion. KI default conflicts (table 20.0 vs tool 90.0).

fields.name: x4 (GR4J unit-hydrograph base time)
fields.notes: UH base time; controls peak timing. KI default conflicts (table 3.5 vs tool 1.7).

fields.model_input_format: hardcoded element defaults in gr4j.py flux equations
fields.name: GR4J fixed shape exponents (alpha=2.0, beta=5.0, ni=4/9, gamma=5.0, omega=3.5)
fields.notes: Canonical GR4J shape constants baked into the production-store, routing-store, and exchange flux equations; not normally calibrated.

fields.name: HBV/HYMOD soil parameters (Smax, Ce, m, beta)
fields.notes: Smax = storage capacity (high sensitivity), beta = runoff partitioning exponent (high sensitivity), Ce = ET correction, m = smoothing coefficient. Smax/beta may be derived from soil databases (HWSD) via pedotransfer.

fields.name: Power/linear reservoir parameters (k, alpha)
fields.notes: k = recession rate coefficient, alpha = power-law outflow exponent (Q = k*S^alpha). KI default for k conflicts (table 0.01 vs tool/example 0.05).

fields.name: Snow reservoir parameters (T0, m, k)
fields.notes: Temperature-threshold snowmelt; applicable only when a Snow Reservoir is in the structure.

fields.name: Catchment area
fields.notes: Used for Node/Network volumetric routing conversion (Q_m3s = Q_mm_d * area_km2 / 86.4); area in m2 instead of km2 breaks routing by ~1e6.

fields.name: Reservoir initial storage (S0)
fields.notes: Typically 0-500 mm, often set ~0.5*Smax with a 1-2 yr warmup. Wrong units (m/cm) produce a long initial transient.

fields.name: Lag-element initial state
fields.notes: MUST be None; the framework auto-sizes the lag-bin array from the lag-time parameter. A pre-allocated wrong-length array crashes the convolution.

fields.model_input_format: list of floats per Node, must sum to 1.0
fields.name: HRU weights (Node)
fields.notes: Fractional weights of parallel Units. Framework does not enforce normalization; weights as percentages (0-100) scale output ~100x.

fields.name: Network topology
fields.notes: Must be an acyclic tree (each node at most one downstream, outlet downstream=None); a cycle hangs the topological solver.

fields.name: ODE approximator choice
fields.notes: Implicit Euler is the recommended/stable choice; Explicit Euler can produce negative storage and NaN for large timesteps.

fields.name: Root finder choice
fields.notes: Pegasus (bracketing) is the default robust choice. Root-finder architecture (python/numba) must match the approximator architecture, validated at construction.

fields.name: Timestep (dt)
fields.notes: Must match the forcing temporal resolution (1.0 daily, 1/24 hourly); a mismatch silently corrupts storage dynamics.

cadence_evidence.value: Unstructured triangular finite-element / finite-volume mesh defined on a SELAFIN geometry; domain must use a metric (projected) CRS, never WGS84 degrees. The four hydrodynamic unknowns (h, u, v, T) are solved simultaneously and volume conservation is reported via the MASS-BALANCE keyword. The closure is hydrostatic-shallow-water mass/momentum balance; it is not a closed surface energy budget. Time-marching is transient with a user-set TIME STEP (typical 0.01-100 s); steady (permanent) and transient regimes are both supported.

cadence_evidence.value: The model is semi-distributed via a topographic-wetness-index (TWI = ln(a/tanB)) histogram within a single lumped subcatchment, NOT a 2-D grid. Mass-balance closure is verified at finalize as bal = sbar + sump - sumae - sumq + sumrz - sumuz and should be near zero. The model has no energy-balance closure: PET enters as an external forcing and actual ET is a demand-side reduction based on the root-zone deficit. Internal units are strictly metres and hours; per-step indexing of the rain/PE arrays requires the inputs.dat header dt to be 1.0.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure is enforced over the basin water budget: the driver assembles a final water mass-balance report from per-component volume accumulators (vol_P/PR/PS/SM/ET/IN/Rg/GW/R). Channel routing additionally carries a momentum treatment whose completeness depends on the wave method (kinematic = friction + gravity only; diffusive adds the free-surface-slope pressure term; dynamic is the full Saint-Venant momentum equation). A surface energy budget is only computed when the energy-balance snowmelt/evaporation components are selected; the default Priestley-Taylor / degree-day paths are demand-side flux calculations, not a closed energy balance. Time-stepping is component-specific; the channel timestep must satisfy CFL (dt <= dx/v_max). The model can also run continuous (multi-season to multi-year) simulations, but the operational case here is event-scale.

fields.notes: Expected in Kelvin; model subtracts 273.15 internally. Non-finite values silently replaced with 288 K inside the loop. Passing Celsius collapses PET to 0 and forces all precip to snow.

fields.name: incoming solar radiation
fields.notes: Drives PET via Rn = srad*0.0864/2.45. Expected W/m2 (~100-300 daily mean); MJ/m2/d or kJ/m2/d mis-units produce catastrophic PET errors. Non-finite values silently replaced with 150 W/m2.

fields.name: layer porosity fraction (layer_porosity)
fields.notes: Per-layer void-space fraction; layer_cap = porosity*LAYER_THICK. Must be <1.0 (percent values inflate capacity 100x).

fields.name: saturated hydraulic conductivity (layer_ks_mm_d)
fields.notes: Default from Rawls/Clapp-Hornberger texture lookup with depth scaling. mm/h instead of mm/d makes percolation 24x too slow.

fields.name: vertical percolation rate coefficients (perc1-3)
fields.notes: L4 percolation is hardcoded to 0.0; only three percolation coefficients are honored by the engine.

fields.name: baseflow recession coefficient (k_base)
fields.notes: Draws L4 down to wilting point (not field capacity); too-low values let L4 grow without bound.

fields.name: PET scale factor (pet_scale)
fields.notes: Linear multiplier on PET; reasonable range [0.3,2.5], typical 0.8-1.5. Hargreaves PET is linearly sensitive to it.

fields.name: basin area
fields.notes: Wrong area unit (ha vs km2) directly biases discharge magnitude.

fields.name: per-layer soil water (sw[4])
fields.notes: Starting far from equilibrium produces a strong first-year transient; first year (2-3 for L4) discarded as spin-up.

fields.name: snow water equivalent (swe)
fields.notes: SWE=0 default; mid-winter start in a snow-dominated basin misses the first spring melt peak.

fields.name: snow/rain and melt temperature thresholds (t_snow, t_melt)

cadence_evidence.value: Per-cell water-balance closure (P = ET + runoff + baseflow + delta storage in soil/snow/canopy/lake) holds always. Per-cell energy-balance closure (Rnet = H + LE + G + delta cold content) holds in full-energy mode; water-balance-only mode skips the explicit surface-energy solver. Cells are closed to lateral exchange. Time step is configurable via MODEL_STEPS_PER_DAY with hard bounds MIN_SUBDAILY_STEPS_PER_DAY=4 (no coarser than 6 h) and MAX_SUBDAILY_STEPS_PER_DAY=1440 (no finer than 1 min).

MSWX yearly files are 3-9 GB each (global coverage). Default max_workers uses all CPU cores (e.g., 113 workers). When 100+ workers each try to read multi-GB files from the same disk, I/O hits 100% and all workers enter D (uninterruptible sleep) state.

cadence_evidence.value: Mass-balance closure applies to the BOD-DO oxygen budget (first-order BOD decay, atmospheric reaeration, and sediment/hypolimnetic oxygen demand). The seasonal temperature model and the 1-D logistic thermocline are prescribed analytic structural forms (sinusoidal in day-of-year, logistic in depth), not a closed surface energy budget. The seasonal DO output uses a steady-state Streeter-Phelps simplification; the time-dependent oxygen- deficit sag solution is a distinct mode. Profile/thermocline outputs are valid only during summer stratification (Jun-Aug NH) given the fixed thermocline depth.

cadence_evidence.value: Prognostic equations are integrated in flux (conservative) form on a hydrostatic-pressure mass coordinate, conserving dry-air mass and the coupled (mu-weighted) scalar variables; positive-definite/monotonic advection options enforce scalar conservation. This is a dynamical-core mass conservation, not a closed column energy budget: surface energy partitioning depends on the chosen land-surface and radiation schemes. Time integration is time-split: a Runge-Kutta 2nd/3rd-order outer step with smaller acoustic/gravity-wave sub-steps; the model timestep is CFL-constrained (rule of thumb dt <= 6*dx_km) unless adaptive time-stepping is enabled. Horizontal grid spacing typically 1-36 km with ~45 terrain-following eta levels; map projection is Lambert conformal (mid-latitudes), Mercator (tropics), polar stereographic (poles), or lat-lon.

cadence_evidence.value: Water mass-balance closes across the coupled cascade: Noah-MP infiltration-excess feeds overland routing; soil-bottom drainage (SOLDRAIN) recharges the conceptual GW bucket; overland, subsurface, and bucket baseflow feed channel routing. LSM column runs at the hourly timestep; overland/subsurface/channel routing run at short sub-grid timesteps (DTRT_TER, DTRT_CH, seconds) constrained by a Courant number near 1.0. Energy balance is closed inside the Noah-MP column only. GWBASESWCRT=0 opens the budget (soil-column sink with no return path), so an active bucket (=1) or pass-through (=2) is required for mass conservation.

Non-additive intensive quantities (DO, temperature, pH) are not mass-conserved — they are volume-weighted averaged on mixing. Overall timestep is user-configurable, but detailed biochemical processes in agricultural surfaces and rivers assume a daily step. Every graph requires at least one Waste node as terminal outlet.

fields.name: aperture b
fields.notes: Calibrated range 1e-6 to 1e-2 m. Cubic law amplifies aperture error quadratically into permeability. v2.6+ supports stress-field-based hydraulic aperture.

fields.name: transmissivity T
fields.notes: Under-documented input path; only permeability is exercised in worked examples.

fields.name: fluid_viscosity
fields.notes: Hardcoded model default 8.9e-4 (water ~20C) when caller does not override; governs Darcy flux = (k/mu)*(dp/L).

fields.name: matrix_porosity
fields.notes: Calibrated range 0.001-0.3; only used when tdrw_flag enabled.

fields.name: matrix_diffusivity
fields.notes: Calibrated range 1e-12 to 1e-9 m^2/s; cm^2/s confusion gives 1e4x retardation.

fields.name: phi (graph-flow velocity porosity)
fields.notes: Hardcoded default 1; edge velocity = flux/phi, so default makes velocity equal Darcy flux and directly scales travel times if not overridden.

fields.name: seed
fields.notes: seed>0 reproducible; seed==0 substitutes a clock-based seed at runtime, making every run a different network.

cadence_evidence.value: Flow solutions are locally mass-conserving (control-volume finite volume in full-physics; Laplacian L*p=b with conserved edge fluxes in graph mode), which is what makes particle tracking well-posed. There is no transient hydrologic timestepping: 'time' enters only as particle travel time (seconds) in the transport stage. Graph mode assumes 1-D flow along intersection segments with complete mixing at intersections and systematically differs (~30%) from full-physics; the two modes' breakthrough and effective-permeability outputs should not be cross-compared directly.

cadence_evidence.value: Domain is an unstructured triangular FEM mesh of a single glacier/ice-shelf footprint in a projected CRS (meters, e.g. EPSG:3031); HybridModel uses a 2D footprint extruded with a vertical dimension. The velocity solve is a diagnostic (elliptic) momentum balance with no time integration; only thickness is time-integrated, conserving mass via the continuity equation (total volume change equals integral of accumulation x dt). Internally the package uses a non-SI MPa-meter-year unit system (stress in MPa, time in years, velocity in m/yr), not SI.

cadence_evidence.value: Water mass-balance closure over a three-level grid hierarchy: L0 (fine physiographic predictors), L1 (hydrological water balance per cell), L11 (river routing). L1/L11 resolutions must be exact integer multiples of L0. ET is a demand-side flux from the selected PET method, not a closed surface energy budget; there is no energy-balance closure.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF runoff time series on HRU/grid; variable name, units, and timestep declared in control file
fields.name: gridded runoff (surface RUNOFF + subsurface BASEFLOW)
fields.notes: mizuRoute expects a runoff RATE in mm/s. Surface runoff and baseflow must be summed before routing (omitting baseflow loses roughly 30-70% of total flow). Driving land-surface models (VIC OUT_RUNOFF+OUT_BASEFLOW, WRF-Hydro SFCRNOFF+UGDRNOFF, mHM) report mm/timestep, so a divide-by-timestep conversion to mm/s is a model input-contract requirement.

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF; variable names configurable via control-file vname_* mappings (HydroCraft seg_id/tosegment, NHDPlus COMID/toComid, MERIT Hydro RIVID/NextDownID)
fields.name: river-network topology (seg_id, tosegment, seg_length, seg_slope, hru_id, hru_seg_id, hru_area, hru_lat, hru_lon)
fields.notes: Defines every reach and its contributing catchment (HRU). tosegment==0 marks an outlet. Topology must be a single connected tree with valid downstream references.
fields.unit: mixed (m for length, m/m for slope, m2 for area)

fields.model_input_format: RPARAM block derived from network NetCDF and parameter namelists; augmented params read only when hydGeometryOption / topoNetworkOption enabled
fields.name: reach hydraulic/geometry parameters (R_SLOPE, R_MAN_N, R_WIDTH, R_DEPTH bankfull, RLENGTH, R_STORAGE, SIDE_SLOPE)
fields.notes: Channel width may be estimated by a Leopold-Maddock power law W=a*A^b; default temperate coefficients are wrong for arid/tropical zones. Minimum reach slope clamped (model floor min_slope=1e-6; operational guidance applies max(slope,1e-4)).
fields.unit: mixed (m/m slope, s/m^(1/3) Manning n, m width/depth, m3 storage)

fields.model_input_format: parameter namelists (IRF_UH / KWT / HSLOPE) and control-file entries; defaults applied uncalibrated (velo~1.0, diff~800)
fields.name: routing-method parameters (wave velocity velo, diffusivity diff, KWT wave-scale, gamma-UH shape/timescale)
fields.notes: IRF prescribed celerity+diffusivity; KWT/MC/DW celerity derived from Manning n and channel geometry. Several solver constants are hardcoded and not user-tunable: Muskingum weighting Y=0.5; KW/DW finite-difference nodes per reach=20; MC nodes=2; KWT particle cap MAXQPAR=20.
fields.unit: velo m/s; diff m2/s; UH shape dimensionless; UH timescale s

fields.model_input_format: NetCDF variables added to network topology + RPARAM reservoir blocks (D03_*, H06_* monthly inflow/demand, HYP_*)
fields.name: lake/reservoir attributes and operation parameters (is_lake, lake_id, lake_area, lake_max_storage, lake_min_storage, d_h_d_a; Doll03/Hanasaki06/HYPE blocks)
fields.notes: Read only when lake routing enabled (is_lake_sim=.True.). lake_model_type selects level-pool/Doll(1), Hanasaki(2), or HYPE(3).
fields.unit: mixed (m2 area, m3 storage, m/m2 height-area derivative)

fields.model_input_format: optional restart NetCDF (QFUTURE, QFUTURE_IRF, per-method wave/particle states, REACH_VOL)
fields.name: reach routing state restart (per-reach discharge, channel volume, wave/particle states, future-runoff queues)
fields.notes: Optional; initializes reach states for a continued run. Absent for a cold start.

fields.model_input_format: control-file route_opt selecting accumulation(0), IRF, KWT, KW-Euler, MC, DW
fields.name: routing method selection (route_opt / routeMethods)
fields.notes: Multiple methods may be active simultaneously; each emits its own routed-discharge variable.

fields.name: hillslope-routing switch (doesBasinRoute) and accumulation switch (doesAccumRunoff)
fields.notes: doesBasinRoute=1 applies the gamma-UH hillslope delay before reach routing; set 0 to avoid double-counting against a driver that already includes hillslope delay (e.g. Lohmann).

fields.name: simulation window and calendar (sim_start, sim_end, dt, calendar)
fields.notes: dt must satisfy CFL (dt < dx/c) for the conditionally stable KW-Euler and DW methods.

fields.model_input_format: control-file is_remap + remap-weight NetCDF (area-weighted grid-to-HRU mapping)
fields.name: spatial remapping enable (is_remap) and remap weights
fields.notes: Required unless runoff units align 1:1 with routing basins. Per-HRU weight sum should be ~1.0; grid and HRU-polygon CRS must match.

fields.name: lake-simulation enable and lake model type (is_lake_sim, lake_model_type)
fields.notes: Enabling without proper network lake flags causes lake routing to silently fail.

fields.model_input_format: control-file qmodOption (direct_insert) + gauge-observation input; water-management reachflux_in/reachvol_in
fields.name: data-assimilation mode (qmodOption) and prescribed water-management fluxes
fields.notes: Optional. Direct-insert DA injects gauge observations into reach state before channel routing; water-management abstraction/target volume coupled into the flux structure read by every routing scheme.

cadence_evidence.value: Routing conserves routed-runoff volume through the network; basin-aggregated routed runoff (basRunoff) vs input runoff ratio should be ~1.0. The optional lake module closes a separate storage water balance S with inflow, outflow, precip, evap, groundwater exchange, and prescribed abstraction/injection. Configurable routing timestep (dt, typically 300-86400 s); daily is the most common operational step. Solver-internal mass-conservation guards exist (outflow capped at 99.9% of available storage+inflow per step).

fields.model_input_format: station CSV column or NetCDF variable tas; valid 200-330 K
fields.name: temp (air temperature)
fields.notes: Internal T0=273.15 K. Values <200 K (e.g. Celsius input) are silently set to NaN by the input filter.

fields.model_input_format: station CSV column (accumulation) or NetCDF variable pr (flux)
fields.name: precip (precipitation)
fields.notes: CSV is per-timestep accumulation; NetCDF is a rate auto-converted to accumulation ONLY when the units attribute is set to kg m-2 s-1. Phase split mutates this field in place (precip rewritten as snowfall+rainfall).
fields.unit: kg m-2 per timestep (CSV) / kg m-2 s-1 (NetCDF rate)

fields.model_input_format: station CSV column or NetCDF variable hurs; valid 1-100%
fields.name: rel_hum (relative humidity)
fields.notes: Fraction (0-1) input is silently set to NaN by the min=1 filter.

fields.model_input_format: station CSV column or NetCDF variable rsds; valid 0-1500 W m-2
fields.name: sw_in (incoming shortwave radiation)
fields.notes: Power units, not energy. Energy units (J/MJ) are 1000-86400x too high.

fields.model_input_format: station CSV column or NetCDF variable wss; valid 0-50 m s-1, runtime floor 0.1 m s-1
fields.name: wind_speed
fields.notes: Drives undercatch correction; km/h input overscales correction ~3.6x.

fields.name: cloud_fraction
fields.notes: Auto-conversion from 0-1 is fragile (only when max<=1 and len>10); used to cloud-adjust shortwave/longwave when interpolation is off.

fields.name: lw_in (incoming longwave radiation)
fields.notes: If absent, longwave is parameterized from temperature/humidity/cloudiness.

fields.name: snow.albedo.max (fresh-snow albedo)
fields.notes: Range 0.75-0.95, default 0.85.

fields.name: snow.albedo.min (old-snow albedo)
fields.notes: Range 0.40-0.65, default 0.55.

fields.name: snow.albedo.cold_snow_decay_timescale
fields.notes: Range 100-1000 h, default 480.

fields.name: snow.albedo.melting_snow_decay_timescale
fields.notes: Range 50-500 h, default 200.

fields.name: snow.albedo.refresh_snowfall
fields.notes: Snowfall rate that resets albedo; default 0.5.

fields.name: snow.thermal_conductivity
fields.notes: Range 0.1-0.5, default 0.24.

fields.name: snow.melt.degree_day_factor
fields.notes: Range 0.5-6.0. Applies ONLY to temperature-index / enhanced-temperature-index melt, not the energy_balance default.

fields.name: meteo.interpolation.temperature.lapse_rate
fields.notes: Order 0.0026-0.0065 K/m; entering K/km values (e.g. 6.5) corrupts elevation gradients.

fields.name: meteo.interpolation.precipitation.lapse_rate
fields.notes: Precipitation elevation gradient.

fields.model_input_format: Arc/Info ASCII Grid dem_{domain}_{resolution}.asc in projected CRS
fields.name: DEM (digital elevation model)
fields.notes: Required. Filename must exactly match domain+resolution. Source: SRTM/ASTER/LiDAR.

fields.name: land cover grid
fields.notes: Required when canopy or ET modules enabled. Source: CORINE/ESA CCI.

fields.model_input_format: Arc/Info ASCII Grid soil_{domain}_{resolution}.asc or YAML
fields.name: soil texture / parameters grid
fields.notes: Required for ET module. Source: HWSD.

fields.name: soil layer thicknesses
fields.notes: Typical [0.1,0.2,0.4,0.8] m; cm input makes soil heat flux 100x off.

fields.model_input_format: stations.csv (CSV meteo mode) or per-file NetCDF attributes
fields.name: station metadata (id, name, x, y, alt)
fields.notes: At least one station must fall inside the grid extent.
fields.unit: x/y in meteo.crs; alt in m

fields.name: snow.swe (initial snow water equivalent)
fields.notes: Default zero (snow-free start).

fields.name: initial snow density / layer structure
fields.notes: g/cm3 input yields effectively massless layers (1000x error).

fields.name: soil temperature profile
fields.notes: surface.temp is seeded from the top soil layer temperature at init.

fields.name: domain
fields.notes: Identifies the catchment and matches input filenames.

fields.name: start_date / end_date
fields.notes: Simulation window, typically a water year.

fields.name: resolution
fields.notes: Must be meters matching DEM cellsize; km input collapses grid to 1-2 cells.

fields.name: timestep
fields.notes: Seconds/minutes/integers are invalid and fatal at config parse.

fields.name: crs (model grid) / input_data.meteo.crs (stations)

fields.name: snow model scheme (multilayer | cryolayers)

fields.name: meteo interpolation method (regression+IDW | fixed/fractional lapse | MicroMet)
canopy.enabled / evapotranspiration.enabled / glaciers.enabled
fields.notes: Enable optional modules; canopy/ET require land cover, ET requires soil texture.

fields.name: meteo.precipitation_phase.threshold_temp
fields.notes: Rain/snow 50%-snow threshold (default 273.65 K); temp or wet-bulb basis.

cadence_evidence.value: Fully distributed on a projected regular grid (typical 10-100 m, 1-3 h). Solves both a snowpack mass balance (SWE, ice/liquid layer content) and a surface energy balance (radiation + turbulent + advective fluxes) for surface temperature and melt. Energy-balance closure applies to the multilayer/cryolayer snow and surface schemes; the temperature-index and enhanced-temperature-index melt options are demand-side flux parameterizations, not a closed surface energy budget. The grid/DEM must use a projected CRS; CSV station coordinates use a separate input_data.meteo.crs (typically WGS84).

cadence_evidence.value: Surface mass-balance closure on the TIN: dz/dt = tectonics + hillslope diffusion + fluvial incision + marine/wave/carbonate deposition + flexure. Spatial discretization is a Triangulated Irregular Network (Delaunay) built from a regular DEM; drainage routing is single-flow-direction (steepest descent) with Braun & Willett O(n) stack ordering. Time integration is adaptive (mindt/maxdt) bounded by a CFL-like stability limit dt <= dx^2/(2*kappa). Coordinates are a projected Cartesian CRS in metres, not geographic lat/lon. No surface energy balance is computed.

cadence_evidence.value: pyGIMLi is a steady-state forward/inverse PDE library, not a conservation-balance simulator: 'closure: none' reflects that there is no mass/energy budget being closed — the forward problem is a discretized FEM/FVM PDE solve and the inverse problem is a regularized Gauss-Newton minimization (data misfit + lambda x regularization), converging on a target chi^2 = Phi_d/N = 1 (data fitted within noise). temporal left empty because no enum value applies: the model resolves one survey snapshot and the iteration loop is the Gauss-Newton optimizer, not a physical time axis.

fields.name: n_ens_members
fields.notes: Source default 24; >=20 required for stable probability estimates, 48-100 for severe-threshold research; 1 = deterministic.

fields.model_input_format: integer number of FFT bandpass spatial scales
fields.name: n_cascade_levels

fields.name: ar_order

cadence_evidence.value: Lagrangian persistence / advection-based evolution: the field is extrapolated along a quasi-stationary motion field and each cascade level is advanced by an AR(2) autoregressive model with stochastic perturbation. Mass is not strictly conserved (semi-Lagrangian interpolation introduces numerical diffusion and overshoots; advected-out pixels are set to a fill value; stochastic noise perturbs intensities). Skill decays with the Lagrangian predictability horizon, typically minutes to ~2-3 hours of lead time. The model operates on a uniform Cartesian radar grid; no surface energy or water budget is closed.

cadence_evidence.value: Each TIN node's hydrologic computations are valid over its associated Voronoi polygon, which is the control volume for mass conservation; flow is routed node-to-node along triangle edges by a finite-difference approach. Mass-balance closure applies to the coupled water column (interception, unsaturated/saturated storage, snowpack, routing); the validation target is P = ET + Q + dStorage closing within ~1% of precipitation. The surface energy balance (net radiation, latent/sensible/ground heat) is solved to drive ET and snow but is a flux computation, not an independently closed energy budget. Time stepping is continuous/event-based with adaptive steps; meteorological/rainfall forcing is ingested at hour-scale METSTEP.
Simulation start/end and time stepping (STARTDATE, ENDDATE, METSTEP, RAINFALL step)
Simulation start/end and time stepping (STARTDATE, ENDDATE, METSTEP, RAINFALL step)

source_evidence.value: Rainfall must be mm/hr; ERA5 mm/day (24x) or CMFD m/s (3.6e6x) silently scale the entire hydrograph with no error raised.

Rainfall rate not in mm/hr; tRIBS expects rainfall in mm/hr. ERA5 provides mm/day (divide by 24), CMFD provides m/s (multiply by 3.6e6). Using raw values without conversion produces hydrographs that are systematically too high or too low with no error message from the model.
; ['tRainfall', 'tHydroM

Temperature in Kelvin instead of Celsius; tRIBS expects temperature in °C. Reanalysis data (ERA5, CMFD) provides temperature in K (~293 K = 20°C). Using K values makes tRIBS think the air temperature is ~293°C, producing enormous ET and preventing snow.
; ['tEvapoTrans', 'tSnowPack', 'tHydroMet']

Atmospheric pressure in Pa instead of mb (hPa); tRIBS expects pressure in mb (hPa). ERA5 provides Pa (×100 larger). Using 101325 instead of 1013.25 corrupts the psychrometric constant calculation, leading to wrong Penman-Monteith ET estimates.
; ['tEvapoTrans']

Soil depth in meters instead of millimeters; HWSD reports bedrock depth in meters. tRIBS expects mm. DEPTHTOBEDROCK=2 means 2mm (not 2m), giving an impossibly thin soil column that saturates from the first rainfall pulse. No error raised.
; ['tHydroModel', 'tCNode']

Saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ks) in m/s instead of mm/hr; HWSD reports Ks in m/s (typical: 1e-6 to 1e-4). tRIBS expects mm/hr (typical: 0.1–200). Using raw m/s values gives Ks ~ 1e-6 mm/hr, meaning essentially zero infiltration capacity.
; ['tHydroModel', 'infiltration']

fields.model_input_format: gridded NetCDF forcing variable (precip), per cell per timestep
fields.name: precipitation
fields.notes: MUST be mm/timestep (mm/day at daily Δt), NOT mm/s or mm/3hr; no internal unit check, so a wrong unit silently scales runoff by up to 86400x.

fields.model_input_format: gridded NetCDF forcing variable (temp), per cell per timestep
fields.name: air temperature
fields.notes: MUST be Celsius, NOT Kelvin; drives snow precipitation-phase split (threshold tt) and degree-day melt. Kelvin values silently break the snow module and PET.

fields.model_input_format: gridded NetCDF forcing variable (pet), per cell per timestep
fields.name: potential (reference) evapotranspiration
fields.notes: Required unless wflow computes PET internally (Penman-Monteith / De Bruin) from individual met variables; if missing or zero, all precipitation becomes runoff.

fields.name: vertical saturated hydraulic conductivity (KsatVer)
fields.notes: Typical 10-10000 mm/day. Units differ across models (VIC mm/s, MODFLOW m/day); cross-model transfer without conversion makes the soil 86400x too permeable.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc per-cell grid (multiplier on KsatVer for lateral subsurface flow)
fields.name: horizontal conductivity fraction (KsatHorFrac)
fields.notes: Sets lateral subsurface saturated conductivity = KsatHorFrac × KsatVer; in practice the primary streamflow calibration parameter.

fields.name: Ksat exponential decay parameter (f)
fields.notes: Exponential decline of saturated conductivity with depth; controls baseflow-vs-quickflow partitioning and recession. Too low → flat baseflow-dominated hydrograph.

fields.name: soil thickness (SoilThickness)
fields.notes: Typical 500-5000 mm; controls total column water storage capacity.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc with a (layer, y, x) dimension
fields.name: Brooks-Corey exponent (c)
fields.notes: Pore-size index; pore-size lambda derived internally as 2/(c-3). MUST carry a layer dimension or wflow raises a 'type InputEntries has no field' (3D-vs-2D) error.

fields.name: saturated / residual water content (θS, θR)
fields.notes: θS > θR required everywhere.

fields.name: compacted infiltration capacity (InfiltCapSoil)
fields.notes: Typical 50-500 mm/day; limits infiltration and thus saturation/infiltration-excess runoff.

fields.name: rooting depth (RootingDepth)
fields.notes: Controls ET extraction depth and soil-moisture availability.

fields.name: canopy/LAI parameters (max canopy storage, LAI, light extinction, canopy gap fraction, crop coefficient)
fields.notes: Drive Gash/modified-Rutter interception and transpiration.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc grids or config defaults (degree-day coeff default 3.75)
fields.name: snow degree-day and threshold parameters (degree-day coefficient, snowfall/melt thresholds, liquid water holding capacity)
fields.notes: HBV temperature-index snow; precipitation phase split at temperature threshold.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc grids or config defaults (initial ice eq. default 5500, ddf default 3.0)
fields.name: glacier parameters (initial ice equivalent, melting threshold, degree-day coefficient, accumulation fraction, glacier area fraction)
fields.notes: Built-in degree-day glacier; GlacierFrac all-zeros silently disables glacier melt.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc per-cell grids (defaults 0.036 river, 0.072 overland when absent)
fields.name: river Manning roughness (N_River) and overland Manning roughness
fields.notes: Controls routed flow velocity and flood-peak timing/magnitude.

fields.name: river/land geometry (slope, river width, bankfull depth, river length)
fields.notes: Placeholder (non-DEM-derived) geometry gives correct timing but 2-3x magnitude error.

fields.name: paved/impervious fraction (PathFrac)
fields.notes: Typical 0-0.3; sets direct-runoff fraction.

fields.name: USLE C cover-management factor
fields.notes: Typical 0.01-0.3 (forest ~0.004, cropland ~0.30, bare ~0.90); near-zero everywhere → silent zero erosion. (sediment model only)

fields.name: USLE K soil-erodibility factor
fields.notes: SI range 0.001-0.1; US-customary values must be ×0.1317 to SI or sediment yield is ~7.6x off. (sediment model only)

fields.name: grain-size fractions (clay/silt/sand/small-agg/large-agg) and river-bed D50
fields.notes: Five grain classes MUST sum to 1.0 per cell or the sediment budget is unclosed. (sediment model only)

fields.model_input_format: instates NetCDF (warm start) or cold_start__flag defaults
fields.name: initial model states (soil/snow/glacier/interception/surface/river storages)
fields.notes: cold_start__flag=true initializes from defaults but the TOML must still declare all 11 state variables under [state.variables].

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc / instates; reservoir storage re-derived from water level on state load
fields.name: initial reservoir water level (waterlevel_reservoir)

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc grid; y-axis MUST be descending (north first)
fields.name: DEM / elevation (wflow_dem)
fields.notes: Ascending y-axis inverts the LDD; wflow internally transposes (y,x) and reverses y.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc, float64 with NaN inactive; river mask 1 = river cell

fields.name: model configuration switches (variant sbm/sbm_gwf/sediment, routing method kinematic vs local_inertial, reservoir__flag, lake__flag, glacier toggle, cold_start__flag)

fields.notes: Typical 50-500 mm/day; limits infiltration and thus saturation/infiltration-excess runoff.

fields.name: rooting depth (RootingDepth)
fields.notes: Controls ET extraction depth and soil-moisture availability.

fields.name: canopy/LAI parameters (max canopy storage, LAI, light extinction, canopy gap fraction, crop coefficient)
fields.notes: Drive Gash/modified-Rutter interception and transpiration.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc grids or config defaults (degree-day coeff default 3.75)
fields.name: snow degree-day and threshold parameters (degree-day coefficient, snowfall/melt thresholds, liquid water holding capacity)
fields.notes: HBV temperature-index snow; precipitation phase split at temperature threshold.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc grids or config defaults (initial ice eq. default 5500, ddf default 3.0)
fields.name: glacier parameters (initial ice equivalent, melting threshold, degree-day coefficient, accumulation fraction, glacier area fraction)
fields.notes: Built-in degree-day glacier; GlacierFrac all-zeros silently disables glacier melt.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc per-cell grids (defaults 0.036 river, 0.072 overland when absent)
fields.name: river Manning roughness (N_River) and overland Manning roughness
fields.notes: Controls routed flow velocity and flood-peak timing/magnitude.

fields.name: river/land geometry (slope, river width, bankfull depth, river length)
fields.notes: Placeholder (non-DEM-derived) geometry gives correct timing but 2-3x magnitude error.

fields.name: paved/impervious fraction (PathFrac)
fields.notes: Typical 0-0.3; sets direct-runoff fraction.

fields.name: USLE C cover-management factor
fields.notes: Typical 0.01-0.3 (forest ~0.004, cropland ~0.30, bare ~0.90); near-zero everywhere → silent zero erosion. (sediment model only)

fields.name: USLE K soil-erodibility factor
fields.notes: SI range 0.001-0.1; US-customary values must be ×0.1317 to SI or sediment yield is ~7.6x off. (sediment model only)

fields.name: grain-size fractions (clay/silt/sand/small-agg/large-agg) and river-bed D50
fields.notes: Five grain classes MUST sum to 1.0 per cell or the sediment budget is unclosed. (sediment model only)

fields.model_input_format: instates NetCDF (warm start) or cold_start__flag defaults
fields.name: initial model states (soil/snow/glacier/interception/surface/river storages)
fields.notes: cold_start__flag=true initializes from defaults but the TOML must still declare all 11 state variables under [state.variables].

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc / instates; reservoir storage re-derived from water level on state load
fields.name: initial reservoir water level (waterlevel_reservoir)
fields.notes: Active when reservoir__flag is set.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc grid; y-axis MUST be descending (north first)
fields.name: DEM / elevation (wflow_dem)
fields.notes: Ascending y-axis inverts the LDD; wflow internally transposes (y,x) and reverses y.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc, float64 with NaN for inactive cells; must be cycle-free
fields.name: local drain direction (wflow_ldd)
fields.notes: Cycles → 'cycles detected in flow graph' fatal; boundary cells must be pits in both numpy- and wflow-space.

fields.model_input_format: staticmaps.nc, float64 with NaN inactive; river mask 1 = river cell
fields.name: subcatchment mask (wflow_subcatch) and river mask (wflow_river)
fields.notes: Inactive cells set to 0 instead of NaN are treated as active zero-parameter cells; all-zero river mask → zero flow.

fields.name: model configuration switches (variant sbm/sbm_gwf/sediment, routing method kinematic vs local_inertial, reservoir__flag, lake__flag, glacier toggle, cold_start__flag)
fields.notes: Select which process and routing modules are active; structural levers.

fields.model_input_format: TOML [time] section (backfilled from NetCDF time axis if absent)
fields.name: simulation window and timestep (starttime, endtime, timestepsecs)
fields.notes: timestepsecs=86400 for daily.

fields.name: lateral/external inflows and abstractions
fields.notes: Optional prescribed inflows/abstractions; outlet discharge itself is an emergent output, not a prescribed BC.

fields.name: reservoir operating parameters (ResMaxVolume, reservoir_area, ResDemand, ResMaxRelease, ResTargetFullFrac, ResTargetMinFrac, outflowfunc, storfunc)
fields.notes: ResMaxVolume in MCM instead of m³ (1e6 too small) → immediate overflow with no regulation; reservoir_area in km² instead of m² → negligible evaporation; reservoir not on a river cell is silently ignored. Active when reservoir__flag is set.

conditional_stages.required_evidence: First determine whether this KI/case supports meaningful calibration. If applicable, record parameter bounds, observations, training/holdout split, objective, optimizer budget and independent validation; otherwise document why it is not applicable.

required_stages.required_evidence: Select a reproducible case, KI implementation/mode, period/site/grid and required input roles; resolve metadata conflicts.
Record OS/architecture, installation command, dependency versions and working model/component version.
Record pack ID/version, allowed distribution, complete file manifest, SHA-256 checks and local receipt; keep access details private.
Check actual variables, units, coverage, calendar/cadence, grid/site, gaps, duplicates and input-role bindings.
Deliberately supply missing, malformed or incompatible inputs and confirm the KI fails clearly before accepting a run; retain the negative-test receipts.
Run this KI's pinned loaders/tools and preserve conversion commands, hashes, input/output manifest and prerequisite ordering.
Execute the selected model or framework component using those inputs; retain exit status, log and output manifest.
Check model-specific acceptance criteria, finite outputs and applicable conservation/reference comparisons; do not equate exit zero with validity.
Select an independent site, domain or component case appropriate to this KI; acquire and prepare its own inputs and validate the end-to-end result without substituting reference-case files.
Repeat from the published pack in a clean project and compare the declared reproducibility criteria.
